title: Ship immich-video-faces spinoff: create GH repo, push 3 repos in order, verify ArgoCD sync
description:
## Background

`immich-video-faces` (face detection app that pulls from Immich's Postgres + REST API) was previously a subdirectory of `talos-private/base/`, deployed as part of the `arr-stack-private` ArgoCD Application. On 2026-07-14 it was lifted out into its own top-level workspace repo (`workspace/immich-video-faces`) so it can be iterated independently while still deploying into the same `media-private` namespace (co-located with immich for in-cluster DNS to `immich-postgres`, etc.).

**All filesystem changes and manifest wiring are DONE and validated locally.** This task is purely the "push in the right order + verify ArgoCD picks it up" execution step. Nothing here requires re-designing — treat it as a runbook.

## What's already been done (do NOT redo)

### `workspace/immich-video-faces/` (new repo, git init'd on `main`, ~101 files staged, uncommitted)
- Full app moved out of `talos-private/base/immich-video-faces/` — 88 originally tracked files + uncommitted mods (Dockerfile, Tiltfile, frontend/**) came along.
- K8s manifests promoted into `k8s/` subdir to match the `catalyst-data` convention (ArgoCD points `path: k8s`). Files in `k8s/`: configmap, cronjob, deployment, ingressroute, kustomization, pvc, service-postgres, service.
- `tilt/kustomization.yaml`: relative path fixed (`../configmap.yaml` -> `../k8s/configmap.yaml`).
- `Tiltfile`: comment updated re: dev.sh location (dev.sh still lives in `talos-private/` and is unchanged).
- Its own `.beads/` dir came along — fresh beads DB, separate from talos-private's.
- `kubectl kustomize workspace/immich-video-faces/k8s/` builds clean.

### `workspace/talos-private/` (detached)
- Removed `- immich-video-faces/` from `base/kustomization.yaml` resources (comment left pointing at the new ArgoCD App).
- Was NOT in the `replacements:` block — no additional unwiring needed.
- `git status` shows 88 deletions + 1 kustomization.yaml edit staged for the spinoff commit.
- `kubectl kustomize workspace/talos-private/base/` still builds clean.

### `workspace/talos-homelab/` (ArgoCD backlink created)
- New file: `infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/immich-video-faces.yaml`
  - Modeled on `catalyst-data.yaml` (HTTPS repoURL, `path: k8s`, `info:` block).
  - Modeled on `arr-stack-private.yaml` for `syncOptions` (`CreateNamespace=false`, `ServerSideApply=true`, foreground prune).
  - `repoURL: https://github.com/TheBranchDriftCatalyst/immich-video-faces.git`, `targetRevision: main`.
  - `destination.namespace: media-private` (same namespace as immich so in-cluster service DNS works).
  - `finalizers: resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io`, retry 5x/5s->3m, prune+selfHeal automated.
  - `part-of: arr-stack-private` label so it groups in the ArgoCD dashboard.
- Added `- immich-video-faces.yaml` to `infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/kustomization.yaml`.
- `kubectl kustomize infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/` builds clean.

## Why ordering matters

ArgoCD reconciles by cloning `repoURL` at `targetRevision`. If talos-homelab is pushed BEFORE the new immich-video-faces repo has a `main` branch, the App goes `ComparisonError` / `Unknown` and needs a manual re-sync after the repo exists. Avoidable by pushing in the order below.

## Runbook (execute in this exact order)

### 1. Create GH repo + push `workspace/immich-video-faces` FIRST
```
cd workspace/immich-video-faces
# Trim before first commit — currently staged:
#   - test.mp4 (63MB) -> move to .gitignore or Git LFS (GitHub warns >50MB, blocks >100MB)
#   - .DS_Store, .venv/, .pytest_cache/, .playwright-mcp/, ~/ -> all should be gitignored
#   - .beads/ -> keep (it's the app's own issue tracker now)
gh repo create TheBranchDriftCatalyst/immich-video-faces --private --source=. --remote=origin
git commit -m "Initial commit: spun out from talos-private"
git push -u origin main
```

### 2. Push `talos-homelab` (creates ArgoCD App -> auto-syncs from repo pushed in step 1)
```
cd workspace/talos-homelab
git add infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/immich-video-faces.yaml \
        infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/kustomization.yaml
git commit -m "Add immich-video-faces ArgoCD Application (spun out of talos-private)"
git push
```

### 3. Commit `talos-private` spinoff (record removal)
```
cd workspace/talos-private
git add -A base/immich-video-faces base/kustomization.yaml
git commit -m "Spin out immich-video-faces to its own repo + ArgoCD app"
git push
```

### 4. Verify ArgoCD adopts the resources cleanly
Because the pods/PVC/service/ingressroute previously existed under the `arr-stack-private` App, ArgoCD may briefly show both Apps claiming the same resources. ServerSideApply + automated prune should resolve this, but verify:
```
kubectl -n argocd get app immich-video-faces -w
argocd app get immich-video-faces
kubectl -n media-private get all -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=arr-stack-private | grep -i ivf   # should be empty
kubectl -n media-private get all -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=immich-video-faces               # should list them
```
If drift/dupes appear: `argocd app get immich-video-faces --refresh`, then `argocd app sync immich-video-faces`. Worst case: `argocd app sync arr-stack-private --prune` then `argocd app sync immich-video-faces`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `TheBranchDriftCatalyst/immich-video-faces` exists on GitHub with `main` branch containing code + `k8s/` manifests
- [ ] `test.mp4` NOT in the first commit (either gitignored or committed via LFS)
- [ ] `workspace/talos-homelab` main pushed with new ArgoCD App manifest
- [ ] `workspace/talos-private` main pushed with immich-video-faces removed from `base/kustomization.yaml` + 88 files deleted
- [ ] `kubectl -n argocd get app immich-video-faces -o jsonpath='{.status.sync.status}'` -> `Synced`
- [ ] `kubectl -n argocd get app immich-video-faces -o jsonpath='{.status.health.status}'` -> `Healthy`
- [ ] Pods running in `media-private` under new App instance label; no duplicate/orphaned resources from `arr-stack-private`
- [ ] Immich UI still reachable (regression check — same namespace shouldn't have been disturbed)
- [ ] Face-detection cronjob visible: `kubectl -n media-private get cronjob | grep -i immich-video-faces`

## Gotchas

- **63MB `test.mp4`** currently staged in new repo. Decide LFS vs. gitignore BEFORE step 1's commit.
- **Namespace stays `media-private`** — do NOT change `destination.namespace`. Immich's Postgres service (`immich-postgres`) is only resolvable in-namespace.
- **`CreateNamespace=false`** is intentional (namespace already exists, owned by arr-stack-private). Do not flip to `true`.
- **arr-stack-private App owns the namespace resource itself** — leave that alone.
- **Local dev (Tilt)** still uses `k3d-bfm-local-dev` cluster spun up by `../talos-private/dev.sh up`. Unchanged.
- **Beads DB** in new repo is fresh. If you want issues on this project, `bd init` inside `workspace/immich-video-faces` and set a prefix (e.g. `IVF`).
- **Prior uncommitted work** (Dockerfile, Tiltfile, frontend/**) moved with the files — first commit includes them. Expected.

## Rollback

If ArgoCD sync fails hard:
1. `argocd app delete immich-video-faces --cascade=false` (delete App, leave resources)
2. Revert talos-private's spinoff commit + re-add `- immich-video-faces/` to `base/kustomization.yaml`
3. `argocd app sync arr-stack-private` (reclaims the ivf resources)
4. Revert talos-homelab's ArgoCD App commit

## Related

- Pattern doc: `workspace/talos-homelab/CLAUDE.md` -> "Adding a New Application (ArgoCD)"
- Reference App: `infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/catalyst-data.yaml` (same shape, different repo)
- Sibling App: `infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/arr-stack-private.yaml` (the App this used to live under)
- Full handoff also mirrored in `workspace/HANDOFF-immich-video-faces-spinoff.md`

title: Root cause meltdowns: Cilium identity bloat (19k stale CRDs) saturates etcd
description:
## Why this issue exists

After 11+ meltdowns over a week, the actual root cause is identified.

## Root cause

Cilium has 19,439 CiliumIdentity CRDs for only 180 live pods. Per-cilium-agent restart, the agent does a LIST that returns 30MB / 9438+ identity objects (etcd log: `apply request took too long, took:107ms, response: range_response_count:9438 size:29733630`). This saturates etcd → apiserver → KubePrism returns EOF mid-response → cilium-agent fatal at startup (`failed to start: ... EOF`) → kubelet restarts cilium-agent → loop.

cilium-operator ALSO crashlooping (189 restarts/20h) so identity GC never completes a 15-min interval.

## Identity pollution composition

| Source | Count |
|---|---|
| Dagster jobs (`dagster/run-id`, `dagster/op`) | ~15k (Dagster was migrated to catalyst-data repo, leaving residue) |
| Velero pod-volume-backup | 2,594 |
| Batch jobs (`job-name`, `batch.kubernetes.io/job-name`) | 18,710 |
| Live pods | 180 |

## Fix (two parts)

1. **Flux values change** — add `labels:` filter to `infrastructure/base/cilium/values.yaml` excluding high-churn labels (`job-name`, `batch.kubernetes.io/*`, `controller-uid`, `pod-template-hash`, `dagster/*`). Stops NEW pollution.
2. **One-shot cleanup script** — delete CiliumIdentity CRDs not referenced by any live CiliumEndpoint. Drops etcd query payload from 30MB → ~50KB. Stops the cascade immediately.

## How to verify

- cilium-agent restart count stops climbing
- cilium-operator restart count stops climbing
- `kubectl get ciliumidentities | wc -l` drops to ~250 (live + system identities)
- etcd `apply request took too long` warnings cease for `/registry/cilium.io/ciliumidentities`
notes:
## Completion (2026-05-30)

**Cleanup**: 19,438 → 150 CiliumIdentities (149 in-use + 1 system-ish).
**Cluster stability**: cilium-agents stable at 144-149 restarts for 90+ min (was every 8 min before). cilium-operator stable at 189 restarts (was crashlooping).
**Etcd**: queries on /registry/cilium.io/ciliumidentities/* now 3KB instead of 30MB.

## Commits

- `bdb89d7` — root-cause fix (label filter, cleanup script, pod-cleanup integration, alerts, dashboard)
- `dc64bd7` — activated Flux management for Cilium (TALOS-ocj)

## Remaining

Awaiting Flux reconcile to apply label filter to live cilium-config. Monitor active.

title: EPIC: HA control plane — promote talos01 + talos06 to CPs (stacked etcd 3-member)
description:
## Why

The 2026-05-27, 2026-05-29 (and the 2026-05-21, 2026-05-22) cluster meltdowns ALL had the same root cause class: **single control plane node + single etcd member + workloads colocated on the CP + Cilium agent on CP is its own apiserver's CNI**. This is "circular dependency with no slack" — a single jitter on talos00 kills the entire cluster.

The architect, cilium expert, and SRE council members all converged on: HA control plane is the **structural** fix. Every other change (memory bumps, probe tuning, webhook policy) is a bandage.

## Target topology

- **3 CPs**: talos00 (192.168.1.54), talos01 (192.168.1.177), talos06 (192.168.1.19)
- **2 workers**: talos02-gpu (192.168.1.144 — GPU stays as pure worker), talos03 (192.168.1.30 — pure worker)
- **Stacked etcd** (3-member raft quorum, can survive 1 node loss)
- After promotion: consider `allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes: false` if workload pressure on CPs is too high (decide based on metrics)

## Sub-tasks (will file as separate issues)

1. Generate new control-plane configs for talos01 and talos06 (`talosctl gen config`)
2. Add a Talos VIP for apiserver HA (e.g. 192.168.1.50 floating among the 3 CPs) — OR ensure KubePrism works (TALOS-kp-debug)
3. `talosctl apply-config` to talos01 and talos06 with CP config (this is a destructive node transition — re-installs the node)
   - **Pre-step: drain & cordon talos01 and talos06**
   - **Pre-step: ensure no irreplaceable PVCs on these nodes**
4. Watch etcd member join — `talosctl etcd members` should show 3 members
5. Re-run KubePrism verification on the 3 CPs
6. Switch Cilium `k8sServiceHost` to VIP or localhost:7445
7. Update CLAUDE.md and docs to reflect new topology
8. File post-cutover validation runbook

## Risks

- **Destructive**: applying CP config to existing worker nodes wipes them (Talos reinstall). Schedule downtime.
- **etcd quorum during transition**: If we promote sequentially, there are moments with 2 members (no quorum loss tolerance). 
- **PVC affinity**: Some workloads have node-affinity to talos01/06 (e.g. NFS provisioner, local-path PVs). Need to migrate.

## Sequencing

- Do AFTER TALOS-kp-debug (we need apiserver-HA reachable from Cilium pods)
- Do BEFORE TALOS-fed-enable (federation + HA is a cleaner story)
- Do AFTER TALOS-cilium-gitops (Cilium needs to be GitOps so reconciles don't race the topology change)

## Acceptance

- `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{...}'` shows 3 control-plane nodes
- `talosctl etcd members` shows 3 healthy members
- Force-kill one CP → cluster stays operational (validated test)
- Cilium agents stay healthy through the transition
- Documentation updated (CLAUDE.md, README, runbooks)
acceptance_criteria:
- 3 healthy CPs, 3-member etcd raft quorum
- Survives 1 CP loss in chaos test
- Cilium points at HA endpoint (VIP or KubePrism)
- Documentation updated
- Post-cutover incident-free for >1 week
notes:
2026-05-30 04:58 UTC PRIORITY ESCALATED P1 → P0.

After 10 meltdowns in ~14 hours, the structural single-CP fragility is no longer
"theoretical risk we should address eventually" — it's the active recurring root
cause. Throttle fix (TALOS-r10) helped (2h uptime vs 1hr previously) but didn't
eliminate. Kernel-capture data confirms it's NOT kernel panics — userspace
disruption on talos00 cascades into cluster-wide outage in a way that 3 CPs would
prevent.

Captured evidence (kernel-capture + alloy-node + Loki dashboard infrastructure
built today during incident response — see TALOS-fa7):
  - Talos kernel healthy through every meltdown (no panic patterns in /var/log/
    kernel-capture/talos00.log across multiple boots)
  - cilium pods restart in BURSTS during recovery from each force-reboot, but
    stable between meltdowns
  - apiserver becomes externally unreachable while talos00 services (etcd, apid,
    kubelet) stay healthy → kube-apiserver static pod isn't serving outside
    requests for some reason

The pre-flight from the runbook (docs/05-runbooks/ha-control-plane-migration.md)
still applies. Heavy state migration needed:
  - MinIO data on talos01 (where Velero backups live!) — MUST migrate before promotion
  - 5+ Postgres databases + Neo4j on talos06 — migrate via pg_dump + restore OR move
    to NFS storage class
  - 1 KubeVirt VM (gaming/Windows gameserver) on talos06 — live migrate or accept
    downtime
  - CoreDNS replica spread (currently 2 replicas, one on each affected node) —
    scale to 3 with anti-affinity before promotion

Next steps when scheduling the HA migration window:
  1. Block out 4-6 hour maintenance window
  2. Backup MinIO contents externally first (don't trust our backups while migrating
     the node holding backups!)
  3. Run pg_dump on all Postgres workloads on talos01/06 to external storage
  4. Follow the runbook step-by-step

This is the actual fix. Filing as P0.

title: Observability for Kyverno + reflector CNPG→dbgate auto-connect machinery
description:
Make silent failures in the CNPG->dbgate auto-connect chain surface (policy stops mutating, secret stops mirroring, a CNPG cluster never appears in dbgate, a controller degrades). Full investigation + ranked plan: docs/investigations/policy-reflection-observability.md

## The invariant (4 stages; a gap at any = silent failure)
For every CNPG Cluster C in ns N: (1) C-app secret exists+labelled cnpg.io/cluster; (2) Kyverno annotates it for reflector; (3) reflector mirrors it into `databases` (fresh reflected-at); (4) Kyverno injects C into dbgate Deployment env CONNECTIONS csv. Stage 4 is the highest value AND the only hop no existing telemetry can see (KSM/Kyverno metrics/PolicyReports cannot read a Deployment's env).

## Key findings
- PolicyReports are the WRONG primary signal: mutate/mutateExisting produce NO background-scan report entries, only admission-event ones -> reports show execution events, not current state. Verified in Kyverno docs.
- Kyverno metrics (per-controller, :8000) = good for controller health + "last admission errored" (kyverno_policy_results, execution-duration, admission_requests, up). Chart 3.8.2 = app 1.18 -> metric is `kyverno_policy_results` (no _total); GROUND vs Mimir before finalizing queries.
- emberstack/reflector exposes NO Prometheus metrics -> observe via mirror annotations (reflected-at/reflected-version freshness+drift) + pod health.

## Ranked plan
1. (HIGHEST) Coverage reconcile CronJob -> pushgateway gauges (per-cluster, all 4 stages) + alerts CoverageGap(warn)/DbgateGap(crit)/ExporterAbsent(crit dead-man). Only thing that closes stage 4. Precedent: vpn-gateway/rotation/cronjob.yaml (alpine/k8s, curl pushgateway.monitoring:9091). Emit policy_reflection_{cnpg_clusters_total,annotated_total,mirrored_total,dbgate_connected_total, coverage_gap{cluster,stage}, last_run_timestamp}. Test CONNECTIONS csv membership (not raw env keys - delete-drift leaves inert orphans).
2. Enable Kyverno chart serviceMonitor on admission/background/reports/cleanup (Alloy auto-discovers) + alerts KyvernoControllerDown/KyvernoPolicyError; fill the already-reserved-but-empty Kyverno row in policy-ops.json.
3. Add CNPG Cluster block to KSM customResourceState (kube-state-metrics/helmrelease.yaml) + rbac.extraRules postgresql.cnpg.io/clusters (cheap inventory + PromQL cross-check).
4. Dedicated policy-reflection-ops dashboard (Full): Kyverno row + coverage row (clusters vs annotated vs mirrored vs dbgate-connected, coverage % gauge, GAPS table) + reflector health row. json/ + resources/ GrafanaDashboard generator; ground vs Mimir.
5. (Optional) KSM secret annotation/label allowlist for pure-PromQL stage 1-3 cross-check.

## Wiring (no new infra)
Alerts = PrometheusRule in v2-otel/baseline-alerts/ -> Alloy mimir.rules.kubernetes -> Mimir Ruler. Routing already severity-based in alertmanager-config CronJob. Pushgateway already scraped by Alloy (honor_labels).

## Tiers
MVP (~1/2 day): items 1+2 = the safety net.
Full: + items 3,4, reflector staleness panels, optional 5.

## File paths
- infrastructure/base/monitoring/policy-reflection-exporter/{cronjob,rbac,kustomization}.yaml (+ monitoring/kustomization.yaml)
- infrastructure/base/kyverno/helmrelease.yaml (<controller>.serviceMonitor.enabled)
- infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/baseline-alerts/policy-reflection-alerts.yaml (+ dir kustomization)
- infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/kube-state-metrics/helmrelease.yaml (CNPG Cluster CRS + rbac.extraRules)
- grafana-dashboards/json/policy-ops.json (fill Kyverno row, MVP) ; json/policy-reflection-ops.json + resources/ (+ kustomization) (Full)

## Risks
Kyverno metric-name version drift; mutateExisting has no background report so CronJob (state reconciler) is required not optional; pushgateway persists stale gauges (dead exporter reads green -> ExporterAbsent/freshness alert mandatory); KSM secret annotation metrics = mild cardinality/annotation-values-as-labels; dbgate delete-drift inert orphans.

Deliverables done: investigation doc committed at docs/investigations/policy-reflection-observability.md. Remaining = implement MVP then Full. Do NOT deploy without grounding queries vs Mimir.
acceptance_criteria: MVP: coverage CronJob pushing per-cluster gauges live in Mimir; CoverageGap/DbgateGap/ExporterAbsent alerts firing correctly (validated by deliberately breaking one stage); Kyverno serviceMonitor scraped (up{job=~"kyverno.*"} present) + KyvernoControllerDown/PolicyError rules loaded in Mimir Ruler. Full: CNPG Cluster CRS metric present; policy-reflection-ops dashboard with GAPS table grounded vs Mimir; reflector pod/staleness panels.

title: Upgrade Flux 2.8.8 → 2.9.4 (unlocks Kustomization spec.ignore)
description:
Flux control-plane upgrade. WHY: v2.9 adds Kustomization .spec.ignore (field-level drift-ignore by JSON Pointer path + target selector) — needed so Kyverno can own dbgate's env without Flux reverting it (TALOS-7jxm dbgate CNPG auto-connect).

Current: flux v2.8.8 (kustomize-controller v1.8.4). Target: v2.9.4 (latest, 2026-08-07).
Target images: source/kustomize-controller v1.9.4, helm-controller v1.6.3, notification-controller v1.9.3.

Bootstrap layout: clusters/catalyst-cluster/flux-system/flux-system/{gotk-components,gotk-sync,kustomization}.yaml. Current components = 4 core (source,kustomize,helm,notification) + 3 NetworkPolicies. NO image-automation/image-reflector.

STEPS (do NOT use stock install.yaml — it adds image-* + source-watcher):
1. Upgrade flux CLI to v2.9.4 (brew upgrade fluxcd/tap/flux, or curl install script pinned to 2.9.4).
2. flux install --version=v2.9.4 --components=source-controller,kustomize-controller,helm-controller,notification-controller --export > clusters/catalyst-cluster/flux-system/flux-system/gotk-components.yaml
3. git diff — confirm ONLY version bumps + new v2.9 fields, same 4 controllers, NetworkPolicies intact.
4. Commit ONLY the gotk-components.yaml (working tree has unrelated parallel work — stay surgical). Push.
5. Flux self-upgrades. Verify: flux version (all v1.9.x), flux get kustomizations (all Ready), controllers 1/1.
6. Confirm .spec.ignore is accepted: kubectl explain kustomization.spec.ignore.

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text: DONE. Flux self-upgraded 2.8.6→2.9.4 via gotk-components swap (commit 7e60014). All 4 controllers on target: source/kustomize v1.9.4, helm v1.6.3, notification v1.9.3, all 1/1 ready. .spec.ignore CONFIRMED present in the Kustomization CRD (kubectl explain shows 'ignore <[]Object>'). Kustomizations re-reconciled 47/50 Ready; the 3 stragglers (argocd/boomtime app, arr-stack postBuild env, gaming VM webhook) are pre-existing app-level issues, NOT upgrade regressions. NOTE: prior commit cf92979 was mislabeled with this message (cp -i declined + swept an unrelated staged minio .bak deletion); real manifest landed in 7e60014. vpn-rotator validates via gluetun /v1/publicip/ip (returns empty) → false rotation failures
description: ROOT CAUSE of the rotator wedge observed 2026-08-06. After PUTting the new server (API update succeeds, tunnel actually changes), the rotator validates the rotation by polling gluetun's control API /v1/publicip/ip. On this cluster that endpoint returns EMPTY ({"public_ip":""}), so validation loops 'VPN validation N/5: no public IP yet' x5 and then marks the server FAILED — even though egress is fully working (proven: gateway egress = 205.147.16.144, a VPN IP, while validation was failing). Every gateway rotation therefore false-fails and cooldowns a healthy server. Fix: validate via ACTUAL egress (curl through the proxy :8080 to an echo/ipify and compare vs HOME_WAN) or via /v1/vpn/status == running, NOT /v1/publicip/ip. Evidence: vpn-rotator logs 2026-08-06T22:39:50-22:40:05. rotation/configmap-script.yaml rotate.py validate step.

title: Harden nebula-sync per adversarial audit (no-wedge, never touch active pod, DNS-safe)
description: Address audit findings: fix the active-pod exclusion (observed synced=4 failed=1), the SYNC_INTERVAL log-expansion anomaly, timeouts/wedge scenarios, RBAC scope, image/pull, resource limits, bad-config-propagation guard. Must be impossible to disrupt DNS.
close_reason: All 6 audit findings fixed + verified live: relabel app=nebula-sync (kills self-target/liveness-crashloop/VIP-phantom-endpoint), bare $SYNC_INTERVAL (interval now 300 not 60), heartbeat-after-backup (liveness re-arms), kubectl --request-timeout + in-cluster kubeconfig (worker reads the lease), password via stdin, STS-only pod selectors. Script extracted to sync.sh via configMapGenerator. Live: primary=pihole-1 synced=4 failed=0, heartbeat fresh, not in VIP endpoints.

title: DR test: simulate failure modes before tagging v1 stable
description: When audit fixes are in: (1) kill active node/pod → DNS + web VIP fail over to another pod (single lease moves, UI follows, no split); (2) verify nebula-sync re-discovers the new active + keeps syncing; (3) kill a standby → zero impact; (4) restart active pod → persistent stats survive (local-path PVC); (5) kill/wedge nebula-sync → DNS unaffected + worker self-heals via liveness; (6) config-change-then-failover → new active has the synced config. Measure DNS blip duration each scenario.
notes: Instrument every scenario with a high-frequency DNS probe against the VIP (dig @192.168.1.240 every ~200ms, 1s timeout, timestamped OK/FAIL) to MEASURE failover downtime precisely (consecutive FAILs × interval = blip duration). Record the number for node-kill and active-pod-delete; expect ~0 for standby-kill and nebula-sync-kill. Acceptance: node-kill DNS blip within an acceptable bound (target: a few seconds, bounded by the L2 lease re-election).
close_reason: DR test passed 8/8. Measured: failover DNS downtime 1.21s (budget 5s), standby-kill 0.00s, nebula-sync-kill 0.00s + self-heals, single L2 lease (no split), PVC survives restart. Jest harness at infrastructure/base/pihole/tests/ prints a measurements summary; destructive scenarios gated behind PIHOLE_DR_DESTRUCTIVE=1.

title: RESUME PIN: add 'username' field ([email protected]) to 1Password mail-relay, then deploy Stalwart
description:
Mailer subsystem is paused here (2026-08-05). State:
- infrastructure/base/mail/ has namespace + ExternalSecret (single-source: pulls relay-username + relay-password from 1Password 'mail-relay') + Flux Kustomization 'mail' (READY).
- ExternalSecret is currently SecretSyncedError because the 'mail-relay' 1Password item has only a 'password' field, not 'username'.

TO RESUME:
1. Add field 'username' = [email protected] to 1Password item 'mail-relay'.
2. Force sync: kubectl annotate externalsecret mail-relay-credentials -n mail force-sync=$(date +%s) --overwrite  (or wait 1h). Verify secret has relay-username + relay-password.
3. Build + deploy Stalwart relay (w5b.2): Deployment/PVC/Service(smtp.mail.svc:25)/IngressRoute(webadmin UI)/NetworkPolicy + config reading relay-username/secret/From from the secret; relayhost smtp.gmail.com:587 STARTTLS; disable DANE/MTA-STS. Iterate config vs pod logs.
4. Wire Authentik (w5b.3) then Alertmanager (w5b.4).

title: Wire Authentik email backend → relay (FIRST) + verify send
description: Add AUTHENTIK_EMAIL__* to authentik helmrelease env (HOST=smtp-relay.mail.svc, PORT=25, USE_TLS=false, USE_SSL=false, [email protected], TIMEOUT=10). No creds needed (relay handles Gmail auth). Redeploy, then trigger a real send: Authentik admin → test email / password-reset flow, confirm arrival. This is the priority — Authentik currently cannot send at all.

title: Provision Google App Password for @knowledgedump.space → 1Password → ESO (mail-relay-credentials)
description: BLOCKER (needs user): on a knowledgedump.space Google Workspace account with 2FA, generate an App Password for 'Mail'. Store in 1Password (item mail-relay, fields username=<[email protected]>, password=<16-char app pw>). Add ESO ExternalSecret 'mail-relay-credentials' in the 'mail' namespace so the relay can SASL-auth to smtp.gmail.com:587. Alt considered: Workspace SMTP relay service (smtp-relay.gmail.com) — needs static egress IP, skip on residential.

title: Deploy Stalwart mail relay (smarthost→Gmail) + web UI in 'mail' namespace
description:
Deploy Stalwart Mail Server (single Rust binary) as the cluster's outbound SMTP relay with its web admin UI. GitOps under infrastructure/base/mail/: Namespace + Deployment + PVC (rocksdb/queue state) + Service (smtp.mail.svc:25 for in-cluster senders) + IngressRoute (webadmin UI at e.g. mail.talos00) + NetworkPolicy (only authentik + monitoring may send) + ESO for admin creds.

CONFIG (verified via Stalwart webadmin docs):
- Outbound → Relay Hosts: create host smtp.gmail.com:587, authUsername=<[email protected]>, authSecret from mail-relay-credentials (secret variant File/EnvironmentVariable), TLS (STARTTLS/implicitTls).
- Outbound → Routing: route external mail via that relay host.
- Outbound → TLS: DISABLE DANE and MTA-STS (required when using a relay).
- Sender identity: [email protected].

WHY Stalwart (not Postal): Postal has NO external-SMTP-relay support (postalserver/postal#48, closed unimplemented) — it delivers DIRECTLY, which fails on residential IP (port 25 blocked, no rDNS). Stalwart supports smarthost relay + ships a web admin UI, so it satisfies UI + Gmail-relay + light/GitOps. Config can be seeded via TOML in a ConfigMap/Secret and/or the web UI.

title: EPIC: Cluster mailer subsystem — self-hosted SMTP relay → Gmail smarthost (knowledgedump.space)
description:
Give cluster apps a reliable way to send email. Architecture (chosen 2026-08-05): an in-cluster Postfix null-client relay in a 'mail' namespace that apps send to cleartext at smtp-relay.mail.svc:25 (no per-app creds, NetworkPolicy-locked), which authenticates once to smtp.gmail.com:587 and sends as @knowledgedump.space. Gives self-hosted control + one shared credential + one From identity, while Google/Workspace handles SPF/DKIM/DMARC/deliverability (knowledgedump.space is already a live Workspace mail domain; CF zone 960eeb4fbbc31b09daac45333e1113e9). Fully self-hosted DIRECT delivery rejected for now: residential port 25 blocked + home-IP reputation = spam/bounce (revisit only with a VPS/static IP + rDNS).

Consumers: Authentik (fix FIRST — currently no email backend, all password-reset/invite/MFA mail silently fails) and Mimir Alertmanager (email receiver; complements TALOS-2pz Discord routing).

Goal state: relay Deployment+Service+NetworkPolicy in git; mail-relay-credentials via ESO/1Password; Authentik + Alertmanager both sending verified email through the relay.
notes: Architecture FINAL (2026-08-05): Stalwart relay → Gmail smarthost, GitOps 100%. Rejected Postal (direct-send only, no external relay — postalserver/postal#48) and fully-self-hosted direct delivery (residential :25 blocked/no rDNS, see w5b.5). Only non-git secret = Gmail app password via ESO/1Password (w5b.1). Consumers: Authentik first (w5b.3), then Mimir Alertmanager (w5b.4, complements TALOS-2pz).

title: Fix kubevirt virt-api webhook cert expired (blocks gaming Flux Kustomization)
description: virt-api certificate expired 2026-06-15, current time 2026-07-21. Gaming Flux Kustomization health check failing: 'x509: certificate has expired'. Windows VM dry-run fails calling webhook virtualmachines-mutator.kubevirt.io. virt-api pods running but admission webhook dead.
close_reason: kubectl delete pod -n kubevirt -l kubevirt.io=virt-api forced pods to re-mount current cert from kubevirt-virt-api-certs secret. virt-operator had been rotating the underlying secret daily (24h duration), and the CA bundles on the mutating/validating webhooks were current (notAfter Jul 27 2026), but the two virt-api pods had last restarted 2026-06-15 and were still serving the pre-rotation cert from memory (that's why the flux error said 'is after 2026-06-15T23:01:44Z'). Fresh pods came up in ~24s and gaming Flux Kustomization went True. Note: kubectl rollout restart does NOT work here — virt-operator reverts the pod template annotation immediately (deployment was auto-managed).

title: Grafana dashboards showing "No data" — metrics pipeline broken
description:
## Why this issue exists

After TALOS-yyt root-cause fix (identity bloat → meltdown cascade), the cluster stabilized but Grafana dashboards still show "No data" across Flux, ArgoCD, and many panels. Metrics pipeline is broken somewhere between scrape targets and Mimir.

## What we know from earlier debugging

- **mimir-nginx returning 502 Bad Gateway**: backend resolution failures (`mimir-ruler.monitoring.svc.cluster.local could not be resolved (110: Operation timed out)`)
- **CoreDNS can't reach apiserver at 10.96.0.1:443** (intermittent i/o timeout + connection refused) — this was likely a downstream symptom of the meltdown cascade. Verify if it's resolved now that cilium-agents are stable.
- **Flux metric scrape config likely missing in alloy** — explains why Flux dashboards specifically show errors
- **Alloy push timeouts to Mimir** — downstream of the DNS issue

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CoreDNS can reach 10.96.0.1 reliably (test from a pod)
- [ ] mimir-nginx 502s stop
- [ ] Alloy successfully pushes to Mimir (check alloy logs)
- [ ] Flux dashboards show data (need flux-system scrape job in alloy config)
- [ ] ArgoCD dashboards show data

## Approach

Re-check first — many of these were downstream of the meltdown cascade. Now that cluster is stable + Flux is running at full concurrency, some may have self-healed. Check current state before assuming pipeline work needed.

## Defer until

Cluster has been stable for several hours after the bandaid reverts (7d66da3). Then investigate.
close_reason: Self-healed (as the issue predicted). Verified 2026-08-07: pipeline healthy — Alloy pushing 3.4M samples/interval to Mimir, mimir-nginx serving queries (no 502s), Flux scraped (gotk_reconcile 212 series), ArgoCD scraped (argocd_app_info 16 series), flux ReconciliationSucceeded (CoreDNS->apiserver fine). All acceptance criteria met. Residual noise (KSM double-scrape dup errors, ~37 code-server pods with no /metrics) tracked separately in TALOS-57t.

title: Cilium identity bloat safety net: alert + dashboard panel + weekly CronJob
description:
## Why this issue exists

TALOS-yyt fixed the immediate Cilium identity bloat (19k → ~150) and added a label filter to stop pollution from job-name/dagster/velero labels. But the label filter is reactive — if a future workload introduces NEW high-churn labels, we'd silently start accumulating again. Need monitoring + a periodic safety net.

## What to add

1. **PrometheusRule alert** in `infrastructure/base/monitoring/prometheus-rules/`
   - `cilium_identities_count > 1000` for 30m → warning
   - `cilium_identities_count > 5000` for 15m → critical
   - Metric source: `cilium_identity` or `cilium_endpoint_state` (verify exact metric name from cilium operator's /metrics endpoint)

2. **Grafana dashboard panel**
   - Add to `infrastructure/base/monitoring/grafana-dashboards/json/talos-cluster-debug.json` (Cluster Health folder) under Cilium section
   - Show: identity count over time + breakdown by namespace
   - Also add: cilium-agent restart rate (which spikes when bloat triggers cascade)

3. **CronJob safety net** (weekly)
   - Run `scripts/cleanup-cilium-identities.sh --yes` weekly
   - Lives at `infrastructure/base/cilium/identity-cleanup-cronjob.yaml`
   - Belt-and-suspenders with Cilium operator's built-in 15m GC

## Why both alert AND cronjob

Alert tells humans "something is generating churn labels — update label filter".
CronJob auto-cleans so meltdowns don't fire while we triage.
close_reason: All 3 pillars satisfied. (1) Alert: cilium-identity-alerts.yaml existed but false-fired (sum(cilium_identity)=1763 vs true ~79 due to per-agent + ~7x scrape dup); fixed expr to max(sum by(pod)(cilium_identity{container=cilium-agent})) in commit 0630c03 — false alert CLEARED, verified via ruler. (2) CronJob: pod-cleanup cron already cleans cilium identities every 2h (CLEANUP_CILIUM_IDENTITIES=true) — exceeds the proposed weekly. (3) Dashboard: identity count + bloat thresholds + trend now live in network-ops dashboard.

title: Investigate: Flux mass reconcile bursts as cilium-killer (Option A applied 2026-05-30)
description:
## Why

Hypothesis (confirmed in part 2026-05-30): synchronized Flux mass-reconcile bursts every 10 min were saturating the single-CP apiserver, causing cilium-agent /healthz probe (which queries apiserver) to time out, kubelet killing cilium, and the cluster-wide cascade we kept seeing.

**The bigger discovery:** the May 22 throttle fix (--concurrent=2) NEVER ACTUALLY APPLIED to the controllers. The patches were in clusters/catalyst-cluster/flux-system/flux-system/kustomization.yaml (inner) but the outer kustomization references gotk-* files DIRECTLY, bypassing the inner kustomization entirely. Verified 2026-05-30: live kustomize-controller deployment args showed only defaults (no --concurrent flag at all). So controllers were running --concurrent=4 (default), --kube-api-qps=50 (default), --kube-api-burst=100 (default) for 8+ days.

## What was applied (commit 4ae00eb 2026-05-30)

Moved patches to the OUTER kustomization where Flux actually processes them. Now LIVE on both controllers:
- `--concurrent=1` (was effectively 4 via default)
- `--kube-api-qps=10` (was effectively 50 via default)
- `--kube-api-burst=20` (was effectively 100 via default)

This serializes all Flux reconciles. ~30 Kustomizations × ~5s each = ~2.5 min parade instead of 75s burst. Apiserver should see flat load.

## What this issue tracks

Observation window. If the hypothesis is right:
- Meltdowns should stop entirely (cluster stays up for days, not hours)
- Cilium agent restart rate should drop to near-zero outside of intentional rollouts
- Operator restart counts (cnpg, virt-operator) should stop climbing

If meltdowns CONTINUE happening:
- Hypothesis wrong, real trigger is something else
- File new investigation with more specific evidence from the kernel-capture + Loki infrastructure
- HA control plane (TALOS-arx) becomes more urgent

## How to verify (LogQL queries via the new dashboard)

```logql
# Cilium agent restart rate (should be ~0)
rate(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="kube-system",container="cilium-agent"}[1h])

# Cluster API readiness over time (should be 100% uptime)
up{job="kubelet"}

# Any new kernel events (should be 0)
sum(count_over_time({job="kernel-capture"} |~ "(?i)(Kernel panic|BUG:|Oops:)" [24h]))
```

Also check the dashboard "Talos Cluster Debug" panel "Cilium Agent Restarts (24h)" — should drop to <5 within 24h if fix works.

## Acceptance

- 24h observation period without a meltdown
- Cilium restart rate <0.1 per hour per pod (~0)
- Document outcome in the post-mortem doc and close TALOS-arx urgency if fix holds

## If hypothesis is wrong

Sub-investigations to file:
- etcd snapshot fsync correlation (TALOS-w4t may still be relevant)
- Cilium `bpf-policy-map-max` exhaustion (we have alerts at 65536, may need bigger)
- Per-Kustomization interval stagger (Option B from the original analysis)
- Move to kube-proxy + Cilium hybrid mode (user previously vetoed, may revisit)

## Refs

- TALOS-arx (HA — still the structural fix even if this throttle works)
- TALOS-fa7 (observability — built the dashboard during this investigation)
- TALOS-xa1 (post-mortem)
- commit 4ae00eb (the actual fix)
- commit a29010d (the May 22 fix that never applied — explained in post-mortem)
acceptance_criteria:
- 24h observation: no meltdown, cilium restart rate near zero
- Outcome documented in post-mortem
- If hypothesis wrong: new investigation filed with specific evidence
notes:
2026-05-30 04:58 UTC UPDATE — MELTDOWN #10 HAPPENED.

The Flux throttle fix (commit 4ae00eb) IMPROVED but did NOT eliminate meltdowns:

  Pre-throttle uptime range: ~30min to 1.5hr
  Post-throttle uptime: 2h 3m (best of the day!) then meltdown #10

Throttle definitely helped (longest stable period of the day) but not sufficient.
This issue can be considered PARTIALLY confirmed:
  - Synchronized Flux reconcile bursts WERE a contributing factor
  - Removing them shifted the meltdown cycle by 30-90 min
  - But there's ANOTHER trigger underneath

Key evidence from meltdown #10:
  - `/var/log/kernel-capture/talos00.log` shows ZERO panic/oops/BUG patterns across
    3 boots (00:59:54, 01:55:53, 02:46:12 START markers). Confirms again: NOT a
    kernel issue. This is happening at userspace layer.
  - Only 2 lines matching "OOM|kill|cilium" in last 3h kernel-capture data for
    talos00. So not OOM either.

Status: keep open as PARTIAL CONFIRM. The remaining trigger investigation moves
to 4 parallel suspects (Flux throttle was suspect 1):
  - Suspect 2 (TALOS-r11): etcd snapshot fsync correlation
  - Suspect 3 (TALOS-r12): Cilium BPF map exhaustion
  - Suspect 4 (TALOS-r13): talos00 memory pressure / GOMEMLIMIT thrash
  - Suspect 5 (TALOS-r14): SPIRE socket deadlock

(Sub-issue IDs to be assigned by the 4 subagents currently producing test scripts
+ PrometheusRules + Grafana panels for each suspect.)

The structural fix (TALOS-arx HA control plane) remains the right answer because
all 4 remaining suspects share the same underlying problem: single-CP fragility
where ANY userspace hiccup on talos00 cascades into cluster-wide outage.

title: EPIC: comprehensive Talos cluster observability (build on alloy-node DaemonSet foundation)
description:
## Why

The 2026-05-29 incident response revealed our cluster observability has significant gaps:

- We discovered talos00 was self-rebooting on kernel oops (`kernel.panic_on_oops=1`) ONLY because we manually inspected `talosctl service etcd` and noticed `Health check successful (19m ago)` — there was no metric or alert telling us the node had rebooted
- We had no record of kernel events leading up to panics (`/var/log` doesn't persist by default; ring buffer wipes on reboot)
- Cilium agent restart counts of 30+/node went unnoticed (no alert)
- 800+ restarts/week on virt-operator / cnpg-operator silent (no alert)
- Operator-managed webhook reverts not observed
- Mimir push from new alloy-node DaemonSet is timing out (`context deadline exceeded` to mimir-nginx) — basic ingest issue we can't see in any dashboard
- No correlation between cluster-wide events (Flux reconciles, helm upgrades, etcd snapshots) and cilium/apiserver behavior

What we did add 2026-05-29 (foundation for this epic):
- `infrastructure/base/monitoring/kernel-panic-capture/` — privileged DaemonSet tailing `/dev/kmsg` to `/var/log/kernel-capture/<node>.log` (Option A persistent), plus netconsole receiver Deployment (Option B live)
- `infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/alloy-node/` — Alloy DaemonSet shipping kernel-capture + netconsole files to Loki with panic-signal labeling
- `infrastructure/base/monitoring/grafana-dashboards/json/talos-cluster-debug.json` — initial Grafana dashboard (filed alongside this issue)

What's missing — this epic's scope:

## Layer 1: Talos-native observability gaps

- **Talos service health as metrics** — `talosctl service` output isn't scraped. apid, etcd, kubelet, machined, etc. all have STATE + HEALTH that we should expose as Prometheus metrics. A small exporter that polls `talosctl get services` and emits `talos_service_state{node, service, state="Running|Failed|..."}` gauges. Currently we'd only notice an apid failure if cluster API breaks.
- **Talos node reboot detection** — `kube-state-metrics` doesn't expose node boot ID changes. We'd need either a custom metric or use the kubelet `boot_id` change as a signal. Alert: `kube_node_info{boot_id}` changes value → fire NodeRebooted alert. (We had to manually grep kubectl events for "Rebooted" today.)
- **Talos extensions inventory** — `talosctl get extensions` content. Useful for tracking what's installed across nodes.
- **machineconfig drift** — what's actually applied vs what should be? Talos has the concept but it's not metric'd.

## Layer 2: Kernel/host observability gaps

- **Kernel ring buffer rotation alerting** — if our /var/log/kernel-capture/<node>.log starts growing >100MB, alert. (Indicates kernel log flood — usually means something bad is happening.)
- **Memory pressure events** — `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.events` per node, exposed as metric. Counts MemPressureLow/High/Critical transitions.
- **conntrack table fill** — `/proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` / `nf_conntrack_max`. node-exporter has `node_nf_conntrack_entries` but we should add an alert when >80% full.
- **TCP socket exhaustion** — `/proc/net/sockstat` TIME_WAIT counts vs `ip_local_port_range`. node-exporter has these too — alert when >80%.
- **NVMe / disk SMART metrics** — node-exporter's `smartmon` collector if enabled. We may not have it.
- **Hardware MCE (Machine Check Exception)** — kernel logs `mce:` lines on hardware faults. Should be a metric counter via Loki LogQL → alert.

## Layer 3: Cilium-specific observability gaps

- **Cilium agent memory usage** — we bumped to 2Gi. Need a per-node gauge tracking actual usage vs limit. Alert when sustained >80%.
- **BPF map utilization** — Cilium exposes these. Several relevant: cilium_bpf_map_pressure, cilium_policy_count, cilium_endpoint_count, cilium_identity_count. We had the policy map exhaustion incident in May — this is essential.
- **Cilium agent restart correlation** — when cilium-agent restarts, what was the trigger? We need a metric joining restart events with what was happening (Flux reconcile? helm upgrade? snapshot CronJob? etc.)
- **KubePrism health** — Talos exposes `KubePrismStatus` resource via talosctl. Convert to metric: `talos_kubeprism_healthy{node}=1|0`.
- **Hubble flows that fail** — drop reasons aggregated. Hubble metrics exist; just need to dashboard them.

## Layer 4: Control plane observability gaps

- **etcd backend commit latency** — `etcd_disk_backend_commit_duration_seconds`. Already scraped (we have kube-prometheus-stack); just needs dashboard panels + alert on >100ms p99.
- **etcd snapshot duration** — we suspected the hourly snapshot was causing meltdowns. The CronJob completion time is observable but the IN-PROCESS fsync latency on etcd isn't directly metric'd.
- **apiserver request latency by verb / resource** — `apiserver_request_duration_seconds`. Dashboard for "top 10 slowest verbs in last hour" — would have helped diagnose Flux load issues.
- **kube-controller-manager / kube-scheduler restart counts** — static pod restart counts. We saw them EXITED during meltdowns but had no historical view.

## Layer 5: Operator / cluster health observability

- **Operator pod restart rate alert** — Already filed under TALOS-txl but specifically for cilium. Extend to ALL operators: cnpg, virt-operator, tempo-operator, kubevirt, NFD, cert-manager. Alert if `rate(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[15m]) > 1/min sustained`.
- **Admission webhook backend health** — TALOS-8fk filed; expand to also alert if webhook backend latency >5s.
- **Flux reconciliation health** — `gotk_reconcile_duration_seconds` and `gotk_reconcile_condition` from Flux. Dashboard + alert if any kustomization is stuck Unknown > 30 min.
- **ArgoCD application health** — argocd has its own metrics; dashboard them next to Flux for one-pane view.

## Layer 6: Logging/Loki gaps

- **Logs from /var/log/audit/kube/ (kube apiserver audit log) → Loki** — currently not shipped. Useful for forensics after incidents.
- **Logs from Talos services (apid, kubelet, machined, etcd) → Loki** — currently we have to `talosctl logs <service>` per node. A Loki source that ships these would let us LogQL-query across nodes.
- **Loki retention tuning** — verify how long these logs are retained. Default may be 7 days; we probably want longer for kernel events.

## Layer 7: Alerting / runbook gaps

- **LogQL alerting rule for panic_signal=true** — TALOS-2pz needs to finish first (Alertmanager + Discord wired)
- **Critical events → Discord summary** — daily digest of restart counts, webhook failures, etc. so we proactively notice degradation before it cascades
- **PagerDuty-style escalation** — for homelab probably overkill but consider Discord @mention for SEV1

## Acceptance (high-level — sub-issues will break this down)

- A "Cluster Health" Grafana folder with at least 4 dashboards:
  - Cluster overview (this is the initial dashboard being filed alongside this epic)
  - Cilium deep-dive
  - Talos node deep-dive (per-node drill-down)
  - Operators health
- All alerts from Layers 1-5 wired into Alertmanager → Discord
- Loki includes kernel-capture, netconsole, kube-audit, Talos service logs
- Mimir scrape lag for new metrics under 30s p99
- One example "kernel panic detected" alert proven end-to-end (manually trigger → see Discord notification within 1 min)

## Sub-issue breakdown to file later

This epic should be broken into ~12-15 sub-issues, one per layer/gap. Start with the highest-leverage ones:
1. Wire Alertmanager + Discord (TALOS-2pz, already filed)
2. LogQL alert for kernel-capture panic patterns (depends on #1)
3. Talos service health exporter
4. KubePrism health metric
5. Cilium BPF map utilization dashboard panels
6. Talos service logs → Loki shipping
7. Node reboot detection alert

## Related issues

- Builds on: TALOS-arx (HA), TALOS-2pz (Alertmanager), TALOS-txl (cilium restart alerts), TALOS-8fk (webhook alerts)
- Companion: the initial Talos cluster debug dashboard being filed alongside this epic
- Spawned from: TALOS-xa1 (2026-05-29 post-mortem)
acceptance_criteria:
- 4+ dashboards in Grafana "Cluster Health" folder
- Alerts from Layers 1-5 wired through Discord
- Loki has kube-audit + Talos service logs
- All 7 layer-issue sub-tasks broken out and prioritized

title: Test hypothesis: shift etcd-snapshot schedule from :00 to :17, observe meltdown correlation
description:
## Why

The 2026-05-29 cognitive council (specifically the network forensics expert) identified the hourly etcd snapshot CronJob as the highest-probability recurring trigger of the control-plane meltdowns:

> `infrastructure/base/backup/etcd-backup.yaml` schedules `talosctl etcd snapshot` against `192.168.1.54` every hour on the hour, with `Forbid` concurrency. `etcd snapshot` triggers an fsync-heavy `BoltDB`-style read of the entire datastore, stalling the etcd write path. While etcd is stalled, kube-apiserver's gRPC client hits the dialTimeout (default 5s) → ... → cascade.

**Yesterday's meltdown timestamp**: ~03:00 UTC (very close to `:00`).
**Today's meltdown timestamp**: ~16:44 UTC (NOT at `:00`).

The pattern is suggestive but not conclusive from 2 data points.

## Test plan

1. ✅ Schedule changed from `"0 * * * *"` → `"17 * * * *"` in `infrastructure/base/backup/etcd-backup.yaml` (commit pending)
2. ✅ Live update via `kubectl apply` for immediate effect (since Flux source is suspended)
3. Manually trigger one snapshot NOW to verify it actually triggers a cluster issue (controlled test)
4. Observe over next 7 days:
   - If next meltdown is at `:17` → hypothesis CONFIRMED → throttle snapshot OR move to a non-CP etcd peer (after HA)
   - If next meltdown is at `:00` → hypothesis WRONG → snapshot is NOT the trigger
   - If no meltdown at all → either we fixed it with other changes, OR the test window wasn't long enough

## Mitigations if confirmed

- Move snapshot to a worker via etcd member API (after HA: `talosctl etcd snapshot --nodes <worker-with-etcd>`)
- Throttle: weekly or every-6-hours instead of hourly
- Compress: use `etcdctl snapshot` with `--snap-count` tuning (Talos may not expose this)
- Stagger across cluster: snapshot one member at a time on different schedules

## Acceptance

- 7 days of observation data captured
- If hypothesis confirmed, mitigation implemented
- Either way, document the result in `docs/06-troubleshooting/2026-05-29-network-meltdown.md`
acceptance_criteria:
- 7-day observation window completed
- Result (confirmed / refuted / inconclusive) documented in post-mortem
- If confirmed: mitigation in place
notes: 2026-05-29 17:42 UTC: ran manual snapshot test (job/test-snapshot-1780076504). Snapshot completed in <6s, API stayed `ok` throughout, etcd stayed healthy, no cilium restarts. Significantly WEAKENS the standalone-snapshot-as-trigger hypothesis. Possible the meltdown trigger only fires under CONCURRENT load (snapshot + Flux burst + something). Continuing 7-day observation; if no meltdown at all in window, attribute to the other 2026-05-29 changes (memory/hubble/liveness/clustermesh). Also discovered: prune command broken (`awk: command not found` in mc image), 312 snapshots vs 168 retention. Filed separately.

title: Permanent GitOps fix for failurePolicy=Ignore on cnpg webhooks (KubeVirt + Tempo done)
description:
## Why

On 2026-05-29, all 33 webhooks across these 6 configs were live-patched via `kubectl patch` to `failurePolicy: Ignore`:

| Config | Webhooks | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `cnpg-mutating-webhook-configuration` | 3 | cnpg operator (runtime-created) |
| `cnpg-validating-webhook-configuration` | 4 | cnpg operator (runtime-created) |
| `tempo-operator-mutating-webhook-configuration` | 1 | tempo-operator (static manifest) |
| `tempo-operator-validating-webhook-configuration` | 2 | tempo-operator (static manifest) |
| `virt-api-mutator` | 4 | KubeVirt operator (CR-driven) |
| `virt-api-validator` | 19 | KubeVirt operator (CR-driven) |

**The cnpg and virt-api patches will revert** the next time their operator reconciles the webhook config (typically within minutes). Tempo's MIGHT also revert depending on the operator behavior.

## Permanent fix per operator

### Tempo (easiest)
Add a kustomize patch in `infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/operators/tempo-operator/kustomization.yaml`:
```yaml
resources:
  - https://github.com/grafana/tempo-operator/releases/download/v0.19.0/tempo-operator.yaml
patches:
  - target:
      kind: MutatingWebhookConfiguration
      name: tempo-operator-mutating-webhook-configuration
    patch: |
      - op: replace
        path: /webhooks/0/failurePolicy
        value: Ignore
  - target:
      kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
      name: tempo-operator-validating-webhook-configuration
    patch: |
      - op: replace
        path: /webhooks/0/failurePolicy
        value: Ignore
      - op: replace
        path: /webhooks/1/failurePolicy
        value: Ignore
```

### KubeVirt (medium)
KubeVirt CR has `spec.customizeComponents.patches` that can patch its child resources. Add to `infrastructure/base/kubevirt/cr.yaml`:
```yaml
spec:
  customizeComponents:
    patches:
      - resourceType: MutatingWebhookConfiguration
        resourceName: virt-api-mutator
        type: json
        patch: '[{"op":"replace","path":"/webhooks/0/failurePolicy","value":"Ignore"}, ...]'
      - resourceType: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
        resourceName: virt-api-validator
        type: json
        patch: '[same, but for all 19 webhooks]'
```

### cnpg (hardest — operator manages webhook at runtime)
cnpg's helm chart doesn't expose failurePolicy directly. Options:
- **A**: Use a post-install Job that runs `kubectl patch` after the operator deploys (will need to also run on operator restarts — kubectl patch is idempotent)
- **B**: Use ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (k8s 1.30+) to wrap or replace the webhook
- **C**: Add namespaceSelector via post-patch (if we can scope to only `databases` namespace, blast radius is small even with Fail)
- **D**: Drop cnpg entirely if not really used (audit first)

**Recommended**: D first (audit), then A (kubectl-patch Job).

## Bonus: namespaceSelector instead of failurePolicy=Ignore

Even better than `Ignore` is `namespaceSelector` that limits the webhook to only the namespaces using the CRDs. Then the webhook never gets invoked for plex/arr/argocd/flux pods at all. Apply this where possible (especially cnpg — should only fire for `databases` namespace).

## Acceptance

- Tempo: kustomize patch in repo, applied, surviving operator reconciles
- KubeVirt: CR `customizeComponents.patches`, applied, surviving
- cnpg: chosen strategy implemented, webhook stays at Ignore
- Verification script in `scripts/`: `check-webhook-policies.sh` confirms all 6 configs at Ignore
acceptance_criteria:
- All 3 webhook owners have permanent kustomize-based or CR-based fix
- Verified by deleting the operator pod and re-checking failurePolicy — it stays Ignore
- Verification script exists and is referenced in safe-restart-cilium.sh preflight
notes: 2026-05-29 progress: KubeVirt portion DONE (commit 92e6306). Used `spec.customizeComponents.patches` in `infrastructure/base/kubevirt/cr.yaml` with JSON patches by webhook index. Verified live: all 4 virt-api-mutator + 19 virt-api-validator webhooks now show `Ignore`. virt-operator applies on reconcile. Tempo portion was done earlier (commit 257b195 — kustomize patch on upstream tempo-operator manifest). Remaining: cnpg — the cloudnative-pg operator creates its webhook config at runtime and the helm chart doesn't expose failurePolicy directly. Options: (A) post-install Job that kubectl patches periodically, (B) ValidatingAdmissionPolicy as overlay (k8s 1.30+), (C) audit if cnpg is actually used and drop if not. Live-patched on 2026-05-29 but cnpg operator may revert. Need to verify.

title: Move Cilium to proper GitOps (currently manual helm template + kubectl apply)
description:
## Why

Cilium is **not** in Flux or ArgoCD. Discovered during 2026-05-29 meltdown analysis:
- `kubectl get helmrelease -A | grep -i cilium` → nothing
- `helm list -A | grep -i cilium` → nothing
- Workflow today: edit `configs/cilium-values.yaml` → run `helm template cilium cilium/cilium -f configs/cilium-values.yaml > configs/cilium-manifest.yaml` → `kubectl apply -f configs/cilium-manifest.yaml`
- The rendered 2969-line `configs/cilium-manifest.yaml` is committed to git but applied manually

This means:
- Cilium config drift is possible (someone edits live, never edits repo)
- Version upgrades require a person running commands
- No reconciliation if the manifest is partially deleted
- No audit trail of who changed what when

## The chicken-and-egg problem (real reason it's not in GitOps)

Cilium IS the CNI. If Cilium isn't running, no pods have network. If Flux/ArgoCD can't network, they can't reconcile Cilium. So Cilium has to be bootstrapped before Flux even exists. Standard solutions:

- **Option A: ArgoCD self-managed Cilium app.** Bootstrap Cilium → install ArgoCD → register Cilium HelmRelease/Application in ArgoCD → ArgoCD now manages future Cilium upgrades.
- **Option B: Flux HelmRelease with `dependsOn: []` and `installCRDs: false`.** Bootstrap with raw manifest, then transition into Flux ownership.
- **Option C: Talos `cluster.inlineManifests`.** Machine config drives Cilium — but requires regenerating machine config to update.

## Recommendation

**Option A (ArgoCD app)**, because:
- Lines up with stated GitOps demarcation (ArgoCD = apps & ad-hoc, Flux = pure infra). Cilium is "platform" but its bootstrap circularity makes it ArgoCD-natural.
- Aligns with existing pattern: ArgoCD already manages cluster-shaped Helm releases.
- Easier "first bootstrap" story: Talos provisions empty cluster → manual Cilium bootstrap → ArgoCD install → ArgoCD takes over.

## What needs to happen

1. Create ArgoCD `Application` for Cilium using existing helm chart repo source
2. Values inline (use the contents of current `configs/cilium-values.yaml`)
3. `syncPolicy: { automated: { selfHeal: true, prune: false } }` — never auto-prune the CNI
4. `argocd app sync cilium` once to take over from manual install
5. Delete or repurpose `configs/cilium-manifest.yaml` (the rendered output is no longer needed)
6. Document the bootstrap-from-scratch path in `docs/05-runbooks/`

## Acceptance

- ArgoCD Application named `cilium` exists, healthy, synced
- Editing `configs/cilium-values.yaml` (or moving to ArgoCD values block) → push → ArgoCD picks up the change → helm upgrade triggered
- `configs/cilium-manifest.yaml` either deleted or marked deprecated
- Bootstrap-from-scratch runbook documented
acceptance_criteria:
- ArgoCD Application `cilium` exists, syncs successfully
- Live edit-push-deploy loop verified
- Bootstrap runbook documents how a future fresh cluster gets Cilium → ArgoCD → ArgoCD-managed Cilium
notes: 2026-05-29 (meltdown #4): Attempted to activate Cilium-in-Flux. `helm upgrade --install --take-ownership` ran (helm release secret `sh.helm.release.v1.cilium.v1` created, status "failed" due to field-manager conflicts with kubectl-client-side-apply on TLS secrets and DS metadata). When Flux source was resumed and Flux started reconciling, the cilium HelmRelease was never created in cluster — Flux's reconcile triggered something (likely the kustomize-controller picking up the new cilium.yaml + ConfigMap-from-values) that caused the Cilium DaemonSet to roll, hit cilium#41108 chicken-and-egg on talos00, apiserver became unreachable, cluster went dark, force-reboot required. Commit `1128b46` keeps the Flux structure in repo as design but does NOT add it to clusters/catalyst-cluster/flux-system/kustomization.yaml — explicitly deferred until TALOS-arx (HA CP) lands.

title: Flip failurePolicy to Ignore on cnpg / virt-api / tempo-operator webhooks
description:
## Why

These three operators' webhooks are currently `failurePolicy: Fail`:
- `databases/cnpg-webhook-service`
- `kubevirt/virt-api`
- `monitoring/tempo-operator-webhook-service`

When their backing pods crash (which has happened twice now — May 21 and May 27), every pod create/update across the entire cluster stalls 10s per webhook waiting for them to time out. Cluster-wide pod admission grinds to a halt.

None of these webhooks are doing safety-critical validation for the rest of the cluster — they only enforce on their own CRDs. There's no reason a broken cnpg operator should block plex from being rescheduled.

## Fix

In each operator's helm values, set:
```yaml
admissionWebhooks:
  failurePolicy: Ignore
  # optional but better: namespaceSelector to scope only to namespaces using their CRDs
  namespaceSelector:
    matchExpressions:
      - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name
        operator: In
        values: [databases]   # or whatever the CRD users are
```

Even better: `namespaceSelector` so the webhook never even gets called for namespaces that don't use the CRDs.

## Files to edit

- `infrastructure/base/databases/cloudnative-pg/helmrelease.yaml` (or wherever cnpg values live)
- `infrastructure/base/kubevirt/` — virt-api webhook (this one is trickier, it's part of the KubeVirt operator's reconciled state; may need to modify the KubeVirt CR's `customizeComponents`)
- `infrastructure/base/monitoring/tempo-operator/` 

## Acceptance

- `kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfigurations,validatingwebhookconfigurations -o jsonpath='{range .items[*].webhooks[*]}{.clientConfig.service.namespace}/{.clientConfig.service.name}{" "}{.failurePolicy}{"\n"}{end}' | grep -E "cnpg|virt-api|tempo-operator"` returns `Ignore` for all
- Synthetic test: scale tempo-operator to 0 → confirm OTHER namespaces can still create pods normally (would have failed before)
acceptance_criteria:
- All three webhooks set to failurePolicy=Ignore (preferably with namespaceSelector)
- Verified via kubectl after Flux sync
- Synthetic test confirms cluster pod admission survives backend operator crash
close_reason: Closed via update

title: PrometheusRule: alert on admission webhooks with broken backends
description:
## Why

THIS IS THE EXACT TRIGGER THAT TOOK US DOWN TWICE (2026-05-21 and 2026-05-27).

A `MutatingWebhookConfiguration` or `ValidatingWebhookConfiguration` with `failurePolicy: Fail` whose backing Service has zero Ready endpoints will block every pod create/update across the cluster after a 10s timeout per webhook. The cluster appears to work but pod admission grinds to a halt.

On both incidents, three webhook configs were broken with no Ready endpoints:
- `databases/cnpg-webhook-service` (failurePolicy=Fail)
- `kubevirt/virt-api` (failurePolicy=Fail)
- `monitoring/tempo-operator-webhook-service` (failurePolicy=Fail)

The `safe-restart-cilium.sh` pre-flight already implements this exact check — port it to a Prometheus alert.

## Rule to add

```yaml
- alert: AdmissionWebhookBackendBroken
  # uses kube-state-metrics: kube_endpoint_address_available + cross-ref with webhook configs
  # simpler: alert when an endpoints object referenced by a webhook has zero ready addresses
  expr: |
    kube_endpoint_address_available{endpoint=~".*webhook.*"} == 0
    or kube_endpoint_address_available{namespace="databases",endpoint="cnpg-webhook-service"} == 0
    or kube_endpoint_address_available{namespace="kubevirt",endpoint="virt-api"} == 0
    or kube_endpoint_address_available{namespace="monitoring",endpoint="tempo-operator-webhook-service"} == 0
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    summary: "Admission webhook backend {{ $labels.namespace }}/{{ $labels.endpoint }} has no Ready endpoints"
    description: |
      If this webhook has failurePolicy=Fail, every pod admission cluster-wide will stall for 10s waiting for it.
      Past incidents: docs/06-troubleshooting/2026-05-21-cilium-cascading-meltdown.md
      Fix: either restart/fix the backing deployment, or temporarily delete the webhook config:
        kubectl delete (mutating|validating)webhookconfigurations <name>
```

Better long-term: use a `kube_admissionwebhook_*` metric if kube-state-metrics emits one, OR build a small exporter that mirrors the safe-restart-cilium.sh logic.

## Acceptance

- Rule deployed
- Test: scale `cnpg` deployment to 0 → alert fires within 5m → restore → alert clears
acceptance_criteria:
- PrometheusRule deployed
- Synthetic test: scale operator to 0 replicas, alert fires within 5m, routes to Discord
- Annotations include link to recovery runbook

title: PrometheusRule: alert on Cilium agent restart count + CrashLoopBackOff
description:
## Why

On 2026-05-27 we found two cilium pods with 1639 and 1620 restart counts — they had been in CrashLoopBackOff for 5+ days without anyone noticing. The cluster was running in a "Cilium half-broken" state the entire time. Plex breaking was our smoke alarm.

## Rules to add

Add to `infrastructure/base/monitoring/kube-prometheus-stack/cilium-alerts.yaml` (new file):

```yaml
- alert: CiliumAgentRestartingFrequently
  expr: rate(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="kube-system",container="cilium-agent"}[15m]) * 60 > 1
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "Cilium agent on {{ $labels.pod }} restarting more than 1x/min for 10m"
    description: "Node {{ $labels.node }} is likely hitting the cilium startup-probe death loop. See docs/06-troubleshooting/2026-05-21-cilium-cascading-meltdown.md"

- alert: CiliumAgentCrashLoopBackOff
  expr: kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{namespace="kube-system",container="cilium-agent",reason="CrashLoopBackOff"} == 1
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    summary: "Cilium agent on {{ $labels.pod }} is in CrashLoopBackOff"
    description: "Pods on this node cannot reach in-cluster service IPs. Recovery: delete the pod to force fresh start. If that fails, reboot the node."

- alert: CiliumAgentRestartedHundredsOfTimes
  expr: kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="kube-system",container="cilium-agent"} > 50
  for: 1h
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "Cilium agent {{ $labels.pod }} has restarted {{ $value }} times — node likely degraded"
```

## Acceptance

- Rules live in repo, applied via Flux/kustomize
- kubectl get prometheusrule -A includes the new rule
- Test: trigger by deleting a cilium pod repeatedly OR by manually editing the metric — alert fires and routes to Discord (depends on alerting wiring)
acceptance_criteria:
- PrometheusRule deployed and visible in Prometheus UI
- Test alert fires to Discord within 10m of synthetic trigger

title: Wire Prometheus Alertmanager to Discord webhook (no alerts route anywhere right now)
description:
## Why

During the 2026-05-27 cluster meltdown we discovered the cluster had been silently degraded for 5+ days:
- Cilium agents on talos02-gpu and talos03 had **1639 and 1620 restarts** (in CrashLoopBackOff)
- Three operators (cnpg, tempo-operator, virt-api) had been crashlooping for 6 days
- We only found out when plex couldn't load libraries

Root cause that nobody noticed: a router/switch restart earlier in the day partitioned the network briefly. Cilium agents on two nodes got stuck in a startup-probe death loop. Pods on those nodes couldn't reach `10.96.0.1` (apiserver ClusterIP). The operators' webhooks have `failurePolicy: Fail`, so every pod admission cluster-wide started slowing → eventually control plane died.

## Current state

- `flux-system/discord-webhook` Secret exists (1Password-synced via ExternalSecrets) and is wired up to Flux + ArgoCD notifications
- **No Alertmanager is deployed**: `kubectl get alertmanager,alertmanagerconfig -A` returns "No resources found"
- The mimir-alertmanager-fallback-config has a no-op `default-receiver` only
- Prometheus + a bunch of PrometheusRules exist (`cluster-baseline-alerts`, velero, etc.) but they fire to nothing

## What needs to happen

1. Decide on Alertmanager source of truth: kube-prometheus-stack's bundled AM (simpler) vs Mimir Alertmanager (already running for Mimir's recording rules). Recommend the bundled one — simpler routing.
2. Enable AM in kube-prometheus-stack helm values
3. Configure receiver: re-use existing `flux-system/discord-webhook` Secret (copy to monitoring namespace via ExternalSecret OR Secret reference) — uses the `webhook_configs` URL pointing at Discord (Discord's webhook format isn't AM-native; either add `prometheus-msteams`/`alertmanager-discord` shim, or use AM's generic `webhook_configs` with a small adapter)
4. Route critical (sev=critical) → Discord, route warning → Discord with throttle
5. Inhibit rules so we don't get spammed when control plane is down (parent alert suppresses children)
6. Test by firing a synthetic alert

## Acceptance

- `kubectl get alertmanager -n monitoring` shows one running
- Firing a test alert (e.g. `amtool alert add testalert severity=critical`) produces a Discord message in #cluster-alerts (or wherever the user wants)
- Document the Discord channel and the secret rotation procedure in `docs/05-runbooks/`

## Notes

- Existing repo: `infrastructure/base/flux-notifications/` is the template pattern for Discord webhook secrets via ExternalSecrets
- `scripts/setup-flux-discord.sh` exists for setup automation reference
- Discord webhooks have a payload format that AM doesn't speak natively; common adapters: [alertmanager-discord](https://github.com/benjojo/alertmanager-discord) or use a generic webhook + bot
acceptance_criteria:
- Alertmanager deployed and reachable
- Discord receiver configured against existing flux-system/discord-webhook (mirrored to monitoring namespace)
- Test alert fires and is visible in Discord
- Inhibit rules in place for cascading-down scenarios
- Runbook documented

title: Promote talos01 + talos03 to control-plane (3-master HA)
description:
Current cluster is single-CP: talos00 only. Any disk corruption, kernel
panic, or hardware failure on talos00 = full cluster outage with no fast
recovery path (UPS-2026-05-09 was this exact scenario).

Per ADR-001 (docs/02-architecture/ADR-001-power-resilience.md), the
recommended HA layout is **talos00 + talos01 + talos03** as control planes,
with talos02-gpu and talos06 remaining pure workers. Rationale:

- talos02 (Intel Ultra 5 + Intel Arc GPU) is too capable to "waste" on CP
- talos06 (Intel Arc GPU node) same reasoning
- talos01 (Ryzen 5800U) and talos03 (Ryzen 5800U, mostly idle per
  docs/05-projects/cluster-optimization/) are strong CP candidates

## Procedure

1. **Generate** new control-plane machine configs for talos01 + talos03:
   ```
   task talos:gen-config   # if existing, OR
   talosctl gen config catalyst-cluster https://192.168.1.54:6443 ...
   ```
   Adjust each to keep the node's IP + factory installer URL +
   schematic with iscsi-tools (and amd-ucode/amdgpu for talos03).

2. **Apply** via `talosctl apply-config` (triggers reinstall + reboot).
   Do ONE at a time, verifying etcd quorum forms before doing the next:
   - First: talos01 → wait for etcd member added, quorum at 2/2
   - Then:  talos03 → wait for etcd member added, quorum at 3/3

3. **Verify**:
   - `kubectl get nodes` shows 3 control-plane roles
   - `talosctl --nodes <each-cp> etcd status` shows all 3 as healthy
   - `talosctl health` returns OK
   - All workloads still running (CP nodes should still accept workloads
     since allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes=true per CLAUDE.md)

4. **Document**: update docs/02-architecture/ with new topology;
   update CLAUDE.md "Multi-Node Cluster" section.

## Test value

After promotion:
- `talosctl --nodes 192.168.1.54 upgrade --preserve=true` should work
  WITHOUT taking down the whole cluster (other CPs absorb the load)
- Rolling Talos upgrades become trivial via upgrade-talos.py
- Disk failure on one CP = cluster keeps running (etcd 2/3 quorum)

## Risks

- Each `apply-config` is a node rebuild — workloads on that node briefly
  disrupted (drain + reboot). Talos handles this for us.
- If etcd quorum doesn't form correctly, we're in worse shape than before.
  Mitigation: take etcd snapshot BEFORE starting (`talosctl etcd snapshot`).
- talos01/talos03 must have their existing extensions preserved (per
  TALOS-6od learnings). Use their existing factory installer URLs.

## Out of scope

- UPS graceful-shutdown integration — separate ticket
- ext4 ephemeral migration (deferred per ADR-001)

Split out from: TALOS-asv
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] etcd snapshot taken before any change (talosctl etcd snapshot)
- [ ] talos01 promoted to control-plane (kubectl shows role)
- [ ] talos03 promoted to control-plane (kubectl shows role)
- [ ] talosctl etcd status shows 3 healthy members from each CP
- [ ] talosctl health returns OK from each CP endpoint
- [ ] All existing workloads still running (no PVC issues)
- [ ] talos01 + talos03 retain their factory installer schematics
      (iscsi-tools, amd-ucode/amdgpu for talos03)
- [ ] Validate a rolling CP upgrade works: upgrade talos01 to a new
      patch version while talos00 + talos03 serve the cluster
- [ ] Documentation updated: docs/02-architecture/ topology + CLAUDE.md
notes: Parent: TALOS-asv (ADR-001 written). Defense-in-depth for non-power failures.

title: UPS graceful-shutdown integration (NUT or SNMP → talosctl shutdown)
description:
Hardware UPS swap is done (TALOS-asv), but the cluster still has no automated
graceful-shutdown path when UPS battery runs low. Without this, the next
power event will replay UPS-2026-05-09: unclean shutdown → XFS corruption →
total state loss on local-path PVCs (TSDB, Grafana, Nexus, MongoDB, etc.).

Per ADR-001 (docs/02-architecture/ADR-001-power-resilience.md), this is the
HIGHEST-LEVERAGE defense — addresses the root cause of the 2026-05-09 outage
directly, even before HA control plane work.

## Approach options

Pick one based on the new UPS's capabilities:

### Option A: SNMP / HTTP webhook (cleanest)
- If the new UPS has a network management card (NMC) — it exposes battery
  state via SNMP or HTTP.
- A small in-cluster pod polls UPS battery level on a CronJob or watcher
  pattern, and on low-battery calls the Talos API to shutdown.
- Auth via talosctl certs mounted as Secret.

### Option B: NUT (Network UPS Tools) on a Pi/external host
- Standard pattern. Pi (or any always-on Linux box) connects to UPS via
  USB, runs NUT server, monitors battery.
- On low-battery, NUT script SSHes to admin host or hits a webhook that
  triggers `talosctl shutdown`.
- More moving parts but works with any USB UPS.

### Option C: NUT client DaemonSet on Talos
- Talos doesn't expose /dev/usb out-of-the-box; would need a system
  extension or a host-network sidecar with special privileges.
- Complicated; only pursue if A and B aren't feasible.

## What to do FIRST

1. Identify the new UPS make/model
2. Check if it has SNMP, HTTP API, or just USB
3. Pick A or B accordingly
4. Build the monitoring component
5. Test by deliberately draining battery to trigger low-battery threshold
   (or simulate via mock signal)

## Out of scope

- Replacing UPS hardware (already done)
- 3-master HA — separate ticket
- ext4 ephemeral filesystem migration (deferred per ADR-001)

Split out from: TALOS-asv
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Identify new UPS model + supported monitoring protocols documented
- [ ] Approach chosen (A/B/C) with rationale recorded in this ticket
- [ ] Monitoring component built and deployed
- [ ] Talos API auth for shutdown verified (talosctl + cert)
- [ ] Test: simulated low-battery triggers graceful shutdown of all 5 nodes
      in the correct order (workers parallel → control plane last,
      same as scripts/shutdown-cluster.sh)
- [ ] Runbook entry added to docs/05-runbooks/ describing manual override +
      testing procedure
notes: Parent: TALOS-asv (ADR-001 written). UPS hardware swap already complete.

title: Cilium BPF policy map overflow + cascading meltdown (2026-05-21)
description:
Following the Talos v1.13.2 upgrade on 2026-05-21, a sequence of cascading failures took the control plane offline for ~40 minutes. Root cause: long-broken opentelemetry-operator (12+ days in CrashLoopBackOff due to orphan ServiceMonitor) whose MutatingWebhookConfiguration was still registered with failurePolicy=Fail. When we restarted the Cilium DaemonSet to apply a separate BPF map-size fix, every new pod admission stalled on the dead webhook, preventing Cilium agents from starting, which broke apiserver networking, which broke everything.

The actual change (BPF map size bump 16384 → 65536) was correct and necessary. The trigger was *how* it was applied (DS rollout restart) interacting with the latent webhook bug.

Full post-mortem: docs/06-troubleshooting/2026-05-21-cilium-cascading-meltdown.md

Commits landed (844aa94):
- configs/cilium-values.yaml + cilium-manifest.yaml: BPF policy map → 65536
- scripts/upgrade-talos.py: pre-flight webhook health check
- scripts/shutdown-cluster.sh: pre-flight webhook health check
- infrastructure/.../otel-operator/helmrelease.yaml: failurePolicy=Ignore + namespaceSelector
