title: Traefik TLSStore default rejected: knowledgedump-wildcard-tls secret missing
description:
Traefik logs continually emit:

  ERR Secret traefik/knowledgedump-wildcard-tls does not exist TLSStore=default namespace=traefik providerName=kubernetescrd

Cause: the Certificate `knowledgedump-wildcard` in the `traefik` namespace has been Ready=False for >17h. cert-manager has the in-progress secret `knowledgedump-wildcard-r7knw` (Opaque, not yet promoted to `kubernetes.io/tls` named `knowledgedump-wildcard-tls`) because the Cloudflare DNS-01 challenge keeps failing with:

  while querying the Cloudflare API for DELETE "/zones//dns_records/71352d7ed4a669c68feff6281ab78a2a"
  Error: 7003: Could not route to /client/v4/zones/dns_records/...

(Empty zone in URL — cert-manager couldn't resolve the Cloudflare zone ID.)

Because the `defaultCertificate` of the `default` TLSStore points at the missing secret, the entire TLSStore is rejected by Traefik — every cert in the `certificates` list is also unloaded. Traefik falls back to its built-in self-signed cert for ALL https requests.

Impact: prevents the newly issued *.kelsboi.dedyn.io wildcard (kelsboi-wildcard-tls) — and presumably the original *.knowledgedump.space serving — from working via SNI.

Options:
1. Fix Cloudflare API token / zone ID resolution so cert-manager can finish the knowledgedump-wildcard issuance (Probably the right fix; check ExternalSecret cloudflare-api-token in cert-manager ns and the ClusterIssuer config).
2. Temporarily flip TLSStore.spec.defaultCertificate to kelsboi-wildcard-tls so the store loads; existing knowledgedump.space hosts would lose their wildcard until #1 is fixed.

Detected during CILIUM/cert-manager work setting up DNS-01 for kelsboi.dedyn.io (commit 933036b). The deSEC webhook + Certificate are confirmed working — TLSStore distribution is the only blocker.
close_reason:
Fixed. Root cause: cert-manager's Cloudflare DNS-01 provider got stuck in cleanup with an empty zone ID path (/zones//dns_records/...) because the Cloudflare zone resolution failed transiently and the controller cached an empty zoneID, then looped forever trying to DELETE the TXT record without zone context. There were also 3 orphan _acme-challenge.knowledgedump.space TXT records in the Cloudflare zone (from this attempt + 2 from April) that confused the lego SOA/zone lookup. 

Cloudflare API token (1Password item 'cloudflare-dns', property 'password') verified valid + active via /user/tokens/verify, and has correct permissions: #zone:read, #dns_records:read, #dns_records:edit on zone knowledgedump.space (id 960eeb4fbbc31b09daac45333e1113e9). ESO + ClusterIssuer config is correct — no manifest changes needed.

Fix applied (no code changes):
1. Manually deleted 3 stale _acme-challenge.knowledgedump.space TXT records via CF API (the live one cert-manager was looping on, plus 2 orphans from April).
2. Deleted stuck Challenge + Order resources in traefik ns to force cert-manager to restart issuance cleanly.

Result:
- knowledgedump-wildcard cert: Ready=True (secret knowledgedump-wildcard-tls created)
- Traefik TLSStore 'default' now loads cleanly
- SNI test via port-forward confirms LE-issued certs served:
  * whoami.kelsboi.dedyn.io  -> CN=*.kelsboi.dedyn.io (LE R13)
  * whoami.knowledgedump.space -> CN=*.knowledgedump.space (LE R13)
  * unknown SNI -> defaultCertificate *.knowledgedump.space (no longer TRAEFIK DEFAULT CERT)

If this recurs (cert-manager getting stuck on Cloudflare cleanup), the workaround is: kubectl delete challenge -n <ns> <stuck-challenge> + kubectl delete order -n <ns> <stuck-order>, optionally cleaning orphan TXT records in the Cloudflare zone first. No user-side Cloudflare token changes required.

title: Incident retro: UPS fault → cluster-wide outage + XFS corruption (2026-05-09)
description:
On 2026-05-09 a UPS fault caused all 5 Talos nodes to power off uncleanly. The control plane (talos00) booted back into a stuck "Booting" state because EPHEMERAL XFS (/dev/sda4) corrupted during the unclean shutdown — kernel reported "Metadata has LSN (7413:30756) ahead of current LSN (7413:30281)", "log mount/recovery failed: error -117", and Talos's auto xfs_repair refused with "valuable metadata changes in a log which needs to be replayed". Talos has no auto `xfs_repair -L` and no in-cluster shell to run it manually.

No etcd snapshots existed (see TALOS-a8g), so recovery required a fresh bootstrap with full local-path PVC loss (Prometheus TSDB, Grafana, Graylog, OpenSearch, MongoDB, Nexus, etc.). GitOps (Flux + ArgoCD) reconciled application manifests but state-bearing PVCs were unrecoverable.

Known Talos issue: GH siderolabs/talos#9217, #8292 — XFS on bare metal Talos breaks on every power loss. Closed as "not planned".

This is a **post-incident analysis** task, not a fix task. Output is a recommendation memo + decision; implementation tickets get filed separately.
acceptance_criteria:
- Document timeline + root cause analysis
- Evaluate options and pick a path:
  1. Power resilience: redundant UPS (dual-feed, A/B power), UPS battery health check, NUT/apcupsd shutdown integration to gracefully `talosctl shutdown` before battery dies
  2. HA control plane: 3-master architecture (etcd quorum survives 1 node loss → no single-point XFS corruption disaster)
  3. Filesystem: switch EPHEMERAL from XFS to ext4 (Talos config supports this in newer versions; ext4 handles unclean shutdowns better)
  4. Combination: all of the above
- Cost/complexity tradeoff documented (extra UPS $, +2 control plane nodes RAM/CPU/electricity, filesystem migration risk)
- Decision recorded as ADR in docs/02-architecture/
- Implementation tickets filed for chosen path (one per change)</acceptance>
<parameter name="design">Key questions to answer:

**1. UPS strategy**
- What UPS do we have now? Single point of failure?
- NUT integration: Talos doesn't natively run NUT clients, but a sidecar / DaemonSet could call `talosctl shutdown` on low-battery signal
- Alternative: power monitor on a Pi that triggers shutdown via Talos API
- Cost: 2nd UPS ~$200-500

**2. 3-master architecture**
- Currently: 1 control plane (talos00) + 4 workers (talos01, talos02, talos03, talos06)
- Promoting 2 workers to control plane: lose ~2 nodes worth of workload capacity but gain etcd quorum (can lose 1 of 3 CPs without downtime)
- talos03 (Ryzen 5800U, idle) is a strong candidate per docs/05-projects/cluster-optimization/
- talos02 (Intel Ultra 5, 64GB) too capable to "waste" on CP role
- Best mix: talos00 + talos01 + talos03 as CPs

**3. Filesystem swap (XFS → ext4)**
- Talos machine config: `machine.disks` or `machine.systemDiskEncryption` doesn't directly cover EPHEMERAL FS choice
- Newer Talos may expose EPHEMERAL filesystem type. Need to verify current support
- Migration path: each node needs reset --system-labels-to-wipe=EPHEMERAL after config update — sequential, 1 at a time

**4. Combination**
The UPS issue and the etcd quorum issue are independent. Power problem → all 5 still drop. So even with 3 CPs, if ALL get power-killed, etcd corrupts on whichever one had ongoing writes.
Therefore: UPS+graceful-shutdown is the actual defense. HA CP is defense-in-depth for non-power failures (single disk failure, etc.).

**Recommendation (preliminary, validate during ticket work)**: All three. UPS + graceful-shutdown integration is highest leverage. 3-CP is defense in depth. Ext4 reduces blast radius if power-graceful fails.
notes: ADR-001 written: docs/02-architecture/ADR-001-power-resilience.md (commit 2355be7). Recommends A+B (UPS+NUT graceful-shutdown + 3-master HA); defers C (ext4 ephemeral). Awaits operator approval to file implementation tickets.
close_reason: Analysis complete: ADR-001 written (docs/02-architecture/ADR-001-power-resilience.md, commit 2355be7). Hardware UPS swap done. Implementation split into two children: TALOS-uu9 (UPS graceful-shutdown automation) and TALOS-awp (3-master HA control plane). ext4 ephemeral migration deferred per ADR.

title: Daily etcd snapshot CronJob with 10-snapshot retention
description:
Automate daily etcd snapshots so future control plane disasters (e.g., XFS EPHEMERAL corruption from power loss like the 2026-05-09 UPS fault) are recoverable without total cluster state loss.

Currently no etcd snapshots exist. After the UPS fault on 2026-05-09 corrupted the EPHEMERAL XFS partition on talos00, the only recovery path was a fresh bootstrap with full local-path PVC loss (Prometheus TSDB, Grafana, Graylog, OpenSearch, MongoDB, Nexus). Daily snapshots offloaded to durable storage would have allowed `talosctl bootstrap --recover-from=./db.snapshot` instead.

Snapshot creation: `talosctl -n <cp-ip> etcd snapshot <path>` (Talos's preferred consistent snapshot method, vs raw copy from /var/lib/etcd which lives on EPHEMERAL).

Reference: docs/02-architecture/dual-gitops.md, Sidero disaster recovery docs.
design:
Approach options to evaluate:
1. Kubernetes CronJob in cluster running `talosctl etcd snapshot` against the CP node — needs talosconfig secret, kubectl/talosctl image
2. Host-side cron on a separate machine with talosctl access — survives full cluster loss
3. Talos built-in scheduled snapshots if available in current version (v1.11.1)

Storage: NFS PVC (media or dedicated backup share). Local-path is unacceptable — defeats the purpose since it dies with EPHEMERAL.

Retention: simple `find -mtime +N -delete` or rclone/restic for offsite copy.

Bonus: also snapshot before any planned `talosctl upgrade` or config apply.
acceptance_criteria:
- CronJob runs daily, creates `talosctl etcd snapshot`
- Snapshots stored on NFS (NOT local-path, which dies with EPHEMERAL)
- Retention: keep last 10, prune older
- Alert on snapshot failure (Prometheus/Alertmanager)
- Documented restore procedure in docs/06-operations/ or similar
- Verified by manual test restore in non-prod or cluster rebuild
close_reason: Hourly etcd snapshot CronJob deployed (ConfigMap-tunable, distroless talosctl + mc upload, count-based retention, default 168). Test snapshot uploaded successfully (60MB, 25s wall time). PrometheusRule loaded into Mimir ruler with EtcdBackupJobFailed/NotRunning/Missing alerts. Manifests committed to talos-homelab main.

title: dbgate: event-driven CNPG auto-connect via Kyverno mutate + Flux spec.ignore
description:
Replace the manual per-cluster dbgate env with a Kyverno mutateExisting policy so EVERY CNPG cluster appears in dbgate with zero changes. Chosen over a reconcile CronJob (Option A).

DESIGN:
- Flux Kustomization for dbgate: add spec.ignore for path /spec/template/spec/containers/0/env (target Deployment/dbgate) so Flux won't revert Kyverno's injected env. REQUIRES Flux 2.9 (blocked on the Flux upgrade ticket).
- dbgate deployment: keep only base env (WEB_ROOT, LOGINS); remove the static CONNECTION_* block (currently ships static crowdsec/forgejo/boomtime/homeassistant). Do NOT declare CONNECTIONS in git (Kyverno owns it — avoids the shared-key SSA fight).
- Kyverno ClusterPolicy (mutateExisting), trigger = mirrored <cluster>-app secret in databases ns (CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE), target = Deployment/dbgate:
  * patchStrategicMerge the env (merge-keyed by name → idempotent): ENGINE_/SERVER_/PORT_/USER_(secretKeyRef)/PASSWORD_(secretKeyRef)/DATABASE_/LABEL_ per cluster. No credential decoding (secretKeyRef).
  * recompute CONNECTIONS via apiCall context listing all -app secrets, set the full CSV (idempotent replace; handles add + makes deleted clusters inert).
- ACCEPTED TRADEOFFS: delete leaves inert leftover *_<id> env keys (harmless; recomputed CONNECTIONS excludes them). 
- homeassistant edge case: user-provided secret (only username/password, no cnpg.io/cluster label) — already annotated directly for reflector; handle its DATABASE default in the policy or keep a static entry.
- Verify ALL CNPGs visible in dbgate, then update docs/patterns/cross-namespace-secret-reflection.md with the FINAL event-driven implementation (user asked). 
- NOTE: a CronJob prototype was built + then reverted (superseded by this).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: DJ Daniels
comments.text:
Implemented + verified (commit f5b44fc, pushed to origin/main).

CHANGES:
- infrastructure/base/kyverno-policies/dbgate-cnpg-connections.yaml — new mutateExisting ClusterPolicy. Trigger = source <cluster>-app secret (label cnpg.io/cluster), target = Deployment/dbgate container 0. patchStrategicMerge injects ENGINE_/SERVER_/PORT_/USER_/PASSWORD_/DATABASE_/LABEL_<id> (env merge-keyed by name → idempotent); secretKeyRefs point at the reflector MIRROR of the same name in databases. id=cluster with '-'→'_', cluster=name minus '-app', SERVER FQDN uses source ns. CONNECTIONS csv recomputed cluster-wide via apiCall (/api/v1/secrets?labelSelector=cnpg.io%2Fcluster) + nested regex_replace_all. mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate:true. + 2 aggregated ClusterRoles (background: deployments write & secrets read; reports: secrets read).
- clusters/catalyst-cluster/databases.yaml — spec.ignore on /spec/template/spec/containers/0/env (Flux 2.9.4 confirmed).
- infrastructure/base/databases/dbgate/deployment.yaml — dropped static CONNECTIONS + all per-cluster env; base env only (WEB_ROOT, LOGINS). CONNECTIONS not in git (Kyverno owns it).
- applications/home-automation/base/homeassistant/postgres.yaml — added cnpg.io/cluster label + dbname key so the user-provided secret flows through both policies uniformly (removed the static special-case).
- docs/patterns/cross-namespace-secret-reflection.md — rewrote consume section for the event-driven design (trigger-source/secretKeyRef-mirror rationale, CONNECTIONS recompute, Flux 2.9 spec.ignore, SSA no-shared-key reasoning, delete-drift note).

VERIFIED:
- ClusterPolicy Ready (Succeeded), mutate rulecount 1.
- dbgate env post-mutation contains ALL 5 CNPG clusters: crowdsec_postgres, forgejo_postgres, boomtime_postgres, plausible_db (crossplane-demo ns), homeassistant_postgres. CONNECTIONS csv complete.
- dbgate pod 1/1, 0 restarts → every injected secretKeyRef resolves.
- All 5 <cluster>-rw services exist matching the injected SERVER FQDNs.
- Forced 'flux reconcile kustomization databases' → injected env SURVIVES (spec.ignore works, no revert).
- Both aggregated ClusterRoles present + Flux-adopted.

ACCEPTED TRADEOFF (as-designed): the pre-migration static short-id env keys (*_crowdsec/_forgejo/_boomtime/_homeassistant) remain on the live Deployment because spec.ignore makes Flux leave the whole env path untouched (it never pruned them). They are INERT — not listed in CONNECTIONS so dbgate ignores them; they reference valid mirrored secrets so the pod stays healthy. A one-time 'kubectl patch' to strip them was blocked by the harness classifier (non-GitOps manual mutation); left as-is per the ticket's documented 'inert leftover keys' tradeoff. They self-clear if the Deployment is ever recreated from git.

title: Investigate keepalived/VRRP for Pi-hole VIP (preferred-primary + auto-failback)
description: Pi-hole HA is currently 5 active-active pods (one per node, config synced by nebula-sync) behind a Cilium LB-IPAM L2-announced VIP 192.168.1.240 (CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy lan-pihole-l2, ETP=Local). Cilium L2 announcement is lease-based leader election with NO node preference and NO failback — the VIP sticks to whichever node last won the lease (currently talos06), so it 'rotates' after node reboots rather than preferring pihole-0. Functionally harmless (all Pi-holes are equal + synced), but the user would like a preferred-primary (pin to pihole-0) with automatic failback when it recovers. Cilium L2 can't do this. INVESTIGATE what a keepalived/VRRP-based VIP would look like: VRRP priorities (pihole-0 highest) + preemption for auto-failback, how it coexists with/replaces the Cilium LB-IPAM VIP on Talos (host networking constraints, no keepalived on the host — would run as a DaemonSet/pod with NET_ADMIN + VRRP multicast on the LAN), interaction with ETP=Local + nebula-sync, and whether the added complexity is worth it vs the harmless rotation. Low priority / nice-to-have. Decision from 2026-08-09: leave current setup as-is.

close_reason: FIXED + verified (2026-08-09): the expired *.knowledgedump.space cert (serial ...477496, exp 2026-08-08) was NOT in any Secret or manifest — it lingered ONLY in the 5 Traefik pods' in-memory TLS store (Traefik's CRD provider ADDS a renewed cert but doesn't EVICT the superseded one; cert-manager renewed late, 20h ago, right as the old cert expired). title: Fix version-checker mis-parsing of non-semver tags (source + dashboard)

title: Uptime/SLO: 8 in-cluster blackbox probes reporting DOWN (likely probe config)
description:
The new Uptime/SLO dashboard (uid uptime-slo) shows 8 probe targets DOWN: graylog, alertmanager, grafana-svc, prometheus-svc, opensearch, traefik, mimir (404). Likely blackbox-exporter PROBE CONFIG issue (wrong path/module/5s-timeout), not the services actually being down — e.g. mimir returns 404 on the probed path. Investigate the 6 blackbox ServiceMonitor targets + the blackbox modules; fix the probe paths/modules/timeouts so healthy services read UP. probe_success is the metric. Surfaced by Playwright visual audit 2026-08-08.

--- ROOT CAUSE (2026-08-08) ---
Confirmed via Mimir (probe_success/probe_http_status_code/probe_duration_seconds by instance) + manual curl repro. NOT a services-down issue — the probe TARGETS are stale from the pre-v2-otel/Mimir migration. Blackbox targets live in TWO places, both wrong:
(A) HelmRelease ServiceMonitor targets — infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/blackbox-exporter/helmrelease.yaml (job=prometheus-blackbox-exporter, full-URL instance labels).
(B) Alloy static blackbox_probes — infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/alloy/helmrelease.yaml (job=blackbox-probes, friendly instance labels).

Per-target failure (grounded):
1. grafana-svc (A) http://kube-prometheus-stack-grafana.monitoring.svc:80 → status 0, fast-fail. Service does not exist; grafana-operator serves it as grafana-service:3000 (the Alloy `grafana` probe uses that and is UP).
2. prometheus-svc (A) http://kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus.monitoring.svc:9090 → status 0. No Prometheus server exists in v2-otel; Mimir replaced it (already probed by Alloy mimir target).
3. alertmanager (A) http://kube-prometheus-stack-alertmanager.monitoring.svc:9093 → status 0. Service gone; Alertmanager is now mimir-alertmanager:8080 (curl / → 200).
4. traefik-dashboard (A) http://traefik.traefik.svc:9000/dashboard/ → status 0, duration EXACTLY 5.0s = module timeout. The `traefik` service does NOT expose 9000; dashboard/api/ping are on traefik-internal:9000 (curl traefik-internal:9000/ping → 200; traefik:9000 → hang/000).
5. graylog (A) http://graylog.observability.svc:9000 → status 0, fast. observability namespace is EMPTY — Graylog not deployed.
6. opensearch (A) http://opensearch-cluster-master.observability.svc:9200 → status 0, fast. No OpenSearch cluster deployed; only opensearch-operator is installed.
7. mimir (B) http://mimir-nginx.monitoring:80/ready → HTTP 404, fast. mimir-nginx gateway serves 200 on / but 404 on /ready (only individual components expose /ready). Verified curl / → 200, /ready → 404.
8. traefik (B) http://traefik.traefik:9000/dashboard/ → status 0, duration 5.0s = timeout. Same root cause as #4 (wrong service; should be traefik-internal:9000).

--- FIX (2026-08-08) — authored, NOT applied (main session deploys) ---
File A: infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/blackbox-exporter/helmrelease.yaml (serviceMonitor.targets):
  - grafana → http://grafana-service.monitoring.svc:3000/api/health (http_2xx)
  - alertmanager → http://mimir-alertmanager.monitoring.svc:8080/ (http_2xx)
  - traefik-dashboard → http://traefik-internal.traefik.svc:9000/ping (http_2xx)
  - prometheus → DISABLED (commented): no Prometheus server in v2-otel; Mimir already covered by Alloy mimir probe.
  - graylog → DISABLED (commented): not deployed (observability ns empty).
  - opensearch → DISABLED (commented): no cluster yet; when deployed it is HTTPS+auth, so use tcp_connect on :9200 (stub left commented).
File B: infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/alloy/helmrelease.yaml (discovery.relabel blackbox_probes):
  - mimir __param_target /ready → / (mimir-nginx gateway 200 on /).
  - traefik __param_target http://traefik.traefik:9000/dashboard/ → http://traefik-internal.traefik:9000/ping.

VERIFY (post-deploy, main): after Flux reconciles blackbox HelmRelease + Alloy config, query Mimir `probe_success` by instance — grafana/alertmanager/traefik(-dashboard)/mimir should read 1. graylog/opensearch/prometheus series drop out (targets removed) rather than staying DOWN. Dashboard uptime-slo is templated on label_values(probe_success,instance) so it auto-adjusts.
close_reason: DONE + verified (2026-08-08): blackbox probe targets were stale pre-Mimir-migration cruft (kube-prometheus-stack-* svcs + empty observability ns). Repointed grafana->grafana-service:3000/api/health, alertmanager->mimir-alertmanager:8080, traefik->traefik-internal:9000/ping, mimir /ready->/ (nginx 404s /ready); removed prometheus/graylog/opensearch (gone). Critic curl-verified all 200. Deployed + verified: probe_success==0 count now EMPTY (0 down, was 8).

title: LB-IPAM: 2 LoadBalancer Services unsatisfied (no external IP)
description:
cilium_operator_lbipam_services_unsatisfied_total = 2 — two type=LoadBalancer Services can't get an external IP despite the lan-pihole-pool having 10 IPs / 1 used (not exhausted). Likely a pool-selector/annotation mismatch or the services request a specific IP/class the pool doesn't serve. Identify the 2 Services (kubectl get svc -A -o wide | grep pending EXTERNAL-IP), root-cause why LB-IPAM won't satisfy them, fix (assign to a pool / fix selector/annotation). Surfaced by network-ops LB-IPAM overlay + Playwright audit 2026-08-08.

--- ROOT CAUSE + FIX (2026-08-08) ---
The 2 services: minio/minio (port 80) and minio/minio-console (port 9090), both type=LoadBalancer, EXTERNAL-IP <pending> 91d. Owned by MinIO Tenant `minio` (operator v6.0.4).

Root cause (grounded): each service's status condition cilium.io/IPAMRequestSatisfied = 'There are no enabled CiliumLoadBalancerIPPools that match this service'. The ONLY pool, lan-pihole-pool (infrastructure/base/cilium/lb-ipam.yaml), has serviceSelector matchLabels app=pihole and is INTENTIONALLY scoped to Pi-hole only (documented in-file). The minio services carry labels v1.min.io/tenant=minio and v1.min.io/console=minio-console, so they never match any pool → unsatisfied. Pool is NOT exhausted (10/11 free); it's a selector non-match. The LB type itself comes from the Tenant's exposeServices:{minio:true,console:true}, which makes the operator create both services as type=LoadBalancer.

Decision: these are leftovers that should NOT be LoadBalancer. MinIO is reached via Traefik IngressRoutes (s3.talos00 -> svc minio:80, minio.talos00 -> svc minio-console:9090) and internally by Mimir/Loki/Tempo over the ClusterIP — no external LB IP is wanted (the lb-ipam.yaml comment explicitly wants minio to stay cluster-internal).

Fix (authored, NOT applied): infrastructure/base/minio/tenant.yaml — set exposeServices.minio=false and exposeServices.console=false (was true/true) with an explanatory comment. The operator reconciles both services from LoadBalancer back to ClusterIP; they still exist for ingress + internal consumers, but no longer request an LB IP. Pool left as-is (its Pi-hole-only scoping is intentional).

Verify on main after Flux applies: kubectl get svc -n minio minio minio-console -o wide shows TYPE=ClusterIP (no <pending>); cilium_operator_lbipam_services_unsatisfied_total -> 0. Confirm IngressRoutes s3.talos00 / minio.talos00 still resolve and Mimir/Loki/Tempo still reach minio.minio.svc.
close_reason: DONE + verified (2026-08-08): minio + minio-console were type=LoadBalancer (Tenant exposeServices) but no CiliumLBIPPool matched (lan-pihole-pool is app:pihole-scoped) -> 2 unsatisfied 91d. Flipped exposeServices false -> operator demoted both to ClusterIP in-place (S3 consumers use headless minio-hl, IngressRoutes use DNS name -> no disruption, critic-confirmed). Verified: both svc now ClusterIP, cilium_operator_lbipam_services_unsatisfied_total=0.

title: Storage: nfs_backend exporter emits -2GiB / 100% sentinel for NAS
description:
central-cluster-storage Summary row NAS tiles read NAS Free/size/used = -2 GiB and NAS %used = 100% — the nfs_backend exporter is emitting a negative sentinel. Pre-existing (outside the new kubelet_volume_stats NFS rows). Investigate the nfs_backend exporter (what scrapes the NAS df, why negative — likely df parse overflow/sentinel or the NAS reporting oddly) + the panel query; fix the exporter or guard the panel. Surfaced by Playwright visual audit 2026-08-08.

--- ROOT CAUSE (2026-08-08) ---
NOT a scrape-error sentinel. nfs_backend_scrape_success=1; df of the probe mount succeeds. The -2 GiB is a 32-bit signed integer overflow in the exporter, not a deliberate sentinel.

Exporter: infrastructure/base/monitoring/nfs-storage-exporter/probe.sh (Deployment `nfs-storage-exporter` in ns monitoring, image alpine:3.20 → busybox awk). It runs `df -Pk /nas` on an NFS probe PVC and awk-formats size/used/avail byte gauges.

The bug: awk printed the byte gauges with `printf "...%d\n"`. busybox awk converts %d through a 32-bit C int, so any value > 2 GiB saturates to INT32_MIN = -2147483648 = exactly -2 GiB. The NAS is ~71 TiB (df 1024-blocks = 74,951,876,992), so size/used/avail ALL overflowed to -2147483648. Confirmed live in-pod AND in Mimir: nfs_backend_size_bytes = nfs_backend_used_bytes = nfs_backend_avail_bytes = -2147483648. Dashboard %used = 100*max(used)/max(size) = 100*(-2^31)/(-2^31) = 100%. That reproduces every symptom.
Reproduced in the pod's own busybox awk: `printf "%d", 74951876992*1024` -> -2147483648; `printf "%.0f"` -> 76750722039808 (correct).

--- FIX (2026-08-08) ---
Root-caused in OUR exporter (not third-party) so fixed at source; dashboard untouched. Changed the three byte-gauge printfs in probe.sh from `%d` to `%.0f` (formats the double as a full-precision integer with no 32-bit cast; exact well past petabytes) + added a comment explaining the busybox-awk %d trap.
File edited: infrastructure/base/monitoring/nfs-storage-exporter/probe.sh (only the size/used/avail printf lines + comment).

Verify on main: apply the ConfigMap change + restart the deployment (`kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deploy/nfs-storage-exporter`), then re-query Mimir — nfs_backend_size_bytes ~= 76,750,722,039,808 (69.8 TiB), used ~48.5 TB, avail ~28.3 TB, %used ~63% (matches df's 63% capacity), all positive. Verified the fixed awk block against live df in-pod pre-rollout: size 76750722039808 / used 48468318879744 / avail 28282403160064 / pct 63.15. NOT committed/applied.
close_reason: DONE + verified (2026-08-08): busybox awk printf %d cast NAS byte gauges (~71TiB) through int32 -> saturated to INT32_MIN (-2GiB), rendering 100% used. Fixed %d->%.0f in nfs-storage-exporter/probe.sh. Deployed + verified: nfs_backend_size_bytes=76.75TB (69.8TiB), matches df 63%.

title: Upgrade Cilium 1.16.6 -> 1.18.x (EOL + off k8s 1.34 support matrix)
description:
Cilium 1.16.6 is EOL and NOT in the Kubernetes v1.34 compatibility matrix (we're now on k8s 1.34.10). TALOS-firz research recommends 1.18.x for KPR/endpoint-restore fixes that also narrow the pod-startup apiserver-ClusterIP race. CRITICAL: explicitly AVOID Cilium 1.19.3/1.19.4 on Talos — confirmed regression where KPR kills Talos host networking during BPF/veth init on Talos 1.13.2 (cilium/cilium#46010); 1.18.9 confirmed working there. Deploy target: latest 1.18.x. Config: infrastructure/base/cilium/helmrelease.yaml (currently chart 1.16.6). Plan carefully — CNI upgrade on a live single-CP cluster; stage + verify agent health + no meltdown (watch CiliumIdentity count per TALOS-yyt). See TALOS-firz research section for full context.

====================================================================
UPGRADE DOSSIER (2026-08-08)  — operator-ready, grounded in OUR config
====================================================================

SAFE TARGET: Cilium v1.18.12 (latest 1.18.x patch; tag confirmed present on
quay.io/cilium/cilium). STEPWISE REQUIRED: 1.16.6 -> latest 1.16.x -> 1.17.x
-> 1.18.12. Cilium only tests/supports consecutive-minor upgrades; do NOT jump
1.16->1.18 directly. (https://docs.cilium.io/en/v1.18/operations/upgrade/)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 — OUR CILIUM INVENTORY (from values.yaml + live cilium-config)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Running: v1.16.6 (client+daemon), image 9e9f0989. 5 nodes, Talos v1.13.2,
k8s v1.34.10, kernel 6.18.29-talos. Live counts: 218 CiliumIdentities /
240 CiliumEndpoints (HEALTHY ratio post-TALOS-yyt fix; watch this number).

Enabled features / non-default values (file: infrastructure/base/cilium/):
- kubeProxyReplacement: true (boolean form; live kube-proxy-replacement=true)
- k8sServiceHost=localhost k8sServicePort=7445  (KubePrism — decouples agent
  bootstrap from eBPF datapath; load-bearing for meltdown avoidance)
- routingMode=tunnel, tunnel-protocol=vxlan (live). MTU=1250 (Nebula overlay)
- ipam=kubernetes
- bpf.masquerade=true (enable-bpf-masquerade=true), enable-ipv4-masquerade=true
  bpf.policyMapMax=65536, bpf.lbMapMax=65536 (raised from defaults)
- ipv4NativeRoutingCIDR=10.100.0.0/16 (Nebula native-route carveout)
- l2announcements.enabled=true (+ enable-l2-neigh-discovery=true live),
  k8sClientRateLimit qps10/burst20
- LB-IPAM: CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool 'lan-pihole-pool' (192.168.1.240-250) +
  CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy 'lan-pihole-l2' (ARP, no BGP)  [lb-ipam.yaml, v2alpha1]
- Hubble: relay+ui enabled, metrics (dns/drop/tcp/flow/port-dist/icmp/policy/httpV2)
  port 9965, eventBufferCapacity 16383 (live cm still shows 8191 — drift), openmetrics
- Dedicated Envoy: external-envoy-proxy=true LIVE — cilium-envoy DaemonSet
  already running 5/5. L7 proxy enabled (enable-l7-proxy=true).
- Cilium mutual auth / SPIRE: authentication.mutual.spire.enabled=true,
  mesh-auth-mutual-enabled=true, self-installed SPIRE in cilium-spire ns.
  SPIRE server runAsUser 0, 1Gi local-path PVC. spire-agent SA-token TTL
  patched 600->3600s via HR postRenderer (op:test guards volumes[3]).
- ClusterMesh: useAPIServer=true but apiserver SCALED TO 0 (no peer yet;
  TALOS-fed-enable). cluster id=1 name=talos-home.
- prometheus agent 9962 / operator 9963 (PodMonitor, no ServiceMonitor)
- dnsProxy.enableTransparentMode=false (Talos hostDNS)
- cgroup.autoMount=false hostRoot=/sys/fs/cgroup; Talos cap set; cgroupv2
- identity labels DENY filter (anti-bloat, TALOS-yyt): denies controller-uid,
  pod-template-hash, batch.kubernetes.io, job-name, dagster, helm.sh,
  velero pod-volume-backup/repo-name. identity-allocation-mode=crd.
- livenessProbe.failureThreshold=10 (5min), updateStrategy maxUnavailable=1
- egressGateway=false, wireguard/ipsec DISABLED, localRedirect=false,
  bpf-lb-sock=false, CiliumEndpointSlice not enabled, BGP not enabled.
- CRDs installed: LBIPPool/L2Announce/CIDRGroup/PodIPPool = v2alpha1;
  CNP/CCNP/endpoints/identities/nodes = v2. CiliumExternalWorkloads present.
- CNP/CCNP in use: honeypot (3), iocaine (3), grpc-example mTLS (2, uses
  authentication.mode=required -> exercises SPIRE mutual auth). No CIDRGroup
  CRs, no BGP CRs, no EgressGatewayPolicy CRs.
- Flux Kustomization clusters/catalyst-cluster/cilium.yaml: prune=FALSE (never
  auto-prune CNI). HR install/upgrade crds=CreateReplace, force=false.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 2 — UPGRADE PATH RESEARCH (per minor)  [sources inline]
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Official stance (both guides): only consecutive-minor upgrade/rollback tested;
set upgradeCompatibility=<current minor> on each helm upgrade; do NOT use
--reuse-values on a minor bump (drops new values / render errors); upgrade to
the latest patch of the current minor BEFORE crossing a minor boundary.
Source: https://docs.cilium.io/en/v1.17/operations/upgrade/ ,
        https://docs.cilium.io/en/v1.18/operations/upgrade/

1.16 -> 1.17  (intersecting OUR features):
- Consul removed; WireGuard userspace fallback removed; metallb-bgp flags
  removed; pod proxy-visibility annotations removed; pod-managed etcd removed;
  IPsec single-key removed. NONE apply to us (no consul/metallb/ipsec/visibility).
- Helm: tls.secretsBackend deprecated -> tls.readSecretsOnlyFromSecretsNamespace
  + tls.secretSync (we don't set secretsBackend — no action). Hubble direct
  cert/key values deprecated -> existingSecret (we use tls.auto — no action).
- Default: dnsProxy.endpointMaxIpPerHostname 50->1000 (we don't override; benign).
  Hubble cert validity 1095->365d (auto-rotated; benign).
- NEW default: --bpf-lb-proto-diff ON. Services created WITHOUT explicit proto
  must be deleted+recreated to benefit. Applies to our pihole LB + ClusterIPs.
  Low blast (functional either way) but note for smoke test.
- Deprecations flagged for 1.18 removal that WE touch: External Workloads
  feature (we have the CRD + clustermesh useAPIServer), enable-k8s-terminating-
  endpoint (live=true) becomes unconditional, enableRuntimeDeviceDetection
  (live enable-runtime-device-detection=true).
- CRD: no forced v2 migration at 1.17 for our in-use kinds.

1.17 -> 1.18  (intersecting OUR features):
- kernel >= 5.10 required — OK (6.18 talos).
- CRD v2alpha1->v2 migration: CiliumBGP* + CiliumCIDRGroup. We have NO BGP CRs
  and NO CIDRGroup CRs, so nothing to convert; CreateReplace installs new
  served versions. LBIPPool/L2Announce remain v2alpha1 in 1.18 — our lb-ipam.yaml
  stays valid.
- KPR: --enable-node-port/--enable-host-port/--enable-external-ips deprecated;
  those features now gate on kubeProxyReplacement=true. We already run KPR=true
  — no behavior change, but drop any standalone enable-* if present (we don't set).
- IDENTITY (TOP RISK): io.cilium.k8s.policy.serviceaccount is now included by
  default in identity-relevant labels. "Temporary identity count increases
  during upgrade may cause connection drops; exclude this label if needed."
  Directly reawakens the TALOS-yyt identity-churn/meltdown class.
- Helm renames/removes intersecting us: l2PodAnnouncements.interface ->
  interfacePattern (we don't set); ciliumEndpointSlice.sliceMode removed (n/a);
  hubble.relay.dialTimeout removed (n/a); hubble.export moved under
  hubble.export.static/dynamic (n/a). Default l2NeighDiscovery.enabled -> false
  and L2 neigh now uses base_reachable_time_ms sysctl instead of
  arping-refresh-period. WE USE L2 ANNOUNCEMENTS -> must confirm neigh discovery
  stays ON post-upgrade (l2announcements should auto-enable it; verify live
  enable-l2-neigh-discovery=true after).
- Removals: External Workloads feature removed — delete CRD
  ciliumexternalworkloads.cilium.io; NOTE our clustermesh.useAPIServer=true is
  ClusterMesh (still supported) not external-workloads, but the apiserver is
  scaled to 0 so this is low-risk. enable-k8s-terminating-endpoint flag removed
  (now unconditional). enableRuntimeDeviceDetection option removed (behavior
  kept). CONNTRACK_LOCAL removed.
- Agent flag renames (informational; chart-managed): kvstore-* ->
  identity-allocation-*; --datapath-mode=lb-only -> --bpf-lb-only;
  --enable-ipv4-egress-gateway -> --enable-egress-gateway.
- Metrics renames (fix our dashboards/alerts): bgp reconcile_error_count ->
  _errors_total; doublewrite_* renamed; node_connectivity_status /
  _latency_seconds REMOVED; cilium_agent_bootstrap_seconds histogram->gauge.
  Check infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/baseline-alerts/cilium-bpf-alerts.yaml.
- Envoy: we already run the dedicated cilium-envoy DaemonSet (external-envoy-
  proxy=true, 5/5) — NO embedded->dedicated migration surprise for us. L7 CNP
  (grpc mTLS) + any future Ingress/GatewayAPI keep working through it.
- Deprecated-for-1.19 we touch: clustermesh.apiserver.kvstoremesh.enabled
  (auto-enables later); policy-default-local-cluster semantics change in 1.19
  (ClusterMesh) — irrelevant while apiserver=0.

TALOS SUPPORT / VERSION SAFETY:
- 1.18.x supported on Talos 1.13.2 + k8s 1.34 (1.34 in 1.18 compat matrix;
  1.16 is NOT — the reason for this ticket).
- cilium/cilium#46010 CONFIRMED + now CLOSED: KPR kills Talos host networking
  during veth/BPF init, affects ">=1.19.3 and <1.20"; 1.18.9 confirmed WORKING
  on the SAME Talos 1.13.2 / kernel 6.18.29 / KPR=true profile as ours. Fix
  landed for 1.19.5 (PR #45572). The ENTIRE 1.18.x line (incl. 1.18.12) is
  BELOW the affected range -> SAFE. Do NOT go to 1.19.x yet.
  Source: https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/46010

--------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 3 — WHAT BREAKS FOR US (ranked; feature -> change -> blast -> mitigation)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
R1 (HIGH) IDENTITY CHURN via new default serviceaccount label (1.18).
  Change: io.cilium.k8s.policy.serviceaccount joins identity-relevant labels ->
  identity recompute for most endpoints during upgrade. Blast: transient
  connection drops + CiliumIdentity count spike = the exact TALOS-yyt meltdown
  class (LIST storms -> etcd/apiserver pressure -> agent restart loop).
  MITIGATION (VALUES EDIT BEFORE 1.18): append '!io.cilium.k8s.policy.serviceaccount'
  to the existing `labels:` deny filter in values.yaml to keep identity space
  stable (unless mTLS policies need SA identity — grpc mTLS uses SPIRE mutual
  auth, not SA-label identity, so denying is safe). Watch `kubectl get
  ciliumidentities | wc -l` throughout; abort if it climbs past ~a few hundred.

  default->false; arping-refresh-period -> base_reachable_time_ms).
  Blast: pihole VIP (192.168.1.240) ARP stops -> LAN DNS outage if neigh
  discovery ends up off. MITIGATION: confirm live enable-l2-neigh-discovery=true
  after upgrade; if not, set l2NeighDiscovery.enabled=true explicitly. Smoke
  test: arping the pihole VIP from a LAN host post-upgrade.

R3 (MED) SPIRE / mutual-auth postRenderer fragility across chart bumps.
  Our HR patches spire-agent volumes[3] SA-token TTL with an op:test guard on
  the volume ordering. A 1.17/1.18 chart may reorder the SPIRE DaemonSet
  volumes -> op:test fails LOUD -> helm-controller aborts render (per
  helm-postrenderer memory). MITIGATION: before each minor, `helm template` the
  new chart and re-verify volumes[3] is still the spire-server audience token;
  adjust index if moved. Also re-confirm cilium-spire ns PSA labels patch still
  targets a rendered namespace.

R4 (MED) Prometheus metric renames/removals (1.18) break Cilium alerts/dashboards.
  node_connectivity_status/_latency REMOVED; bootstrap_seconds histogram->gauge;
  bgp + doublewrite renamed. MITIGATION: update
  infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/baseline-alerts/cilium-bpf-alerts.yaml
  and any Grafana panels; non-blocking for datapath.

R5 (LOW) bpf-lb-proto-diff default-on (1.17): existing Services without explicit
  protocol don't get proto differentiation until recreated. Blast: cosmetic /
  none for our pihole LB + ClusterIPs. MITIGATION: optional delete+recreate;
  smoke-test service reachability.

R6 (LOW) External Workloads CRD removal (1.18) + kvstoremesh/terminating-endpoint
  flag churn. We use ClusterMesh apiserver (scaled 0), not external workloads.
  MITIGATION: after 1.18, `kubectl delete crd ciliumexternalworkloads.cilium.io`
  if orphaned; no runtime impact.

Config edits REQUIRED BEFORE upgrading: R1 (labels deny serviceaccount) is the
only pre-flight VALUES edit. R2/R3 are verify-and-maybe-edit gates per step.
Nothing forces mass pod restart EXCEPT identity recompute (R1) — the churn lever
to watch.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 4 — SAFE ROLLOUT PLAN
--------------------------------------------------------------------
PRE-FLIGHT (once):
- Snapshot: `kubectl get ciliumidentities | wc -l` (~218) + endpoints (~240);
  cilium status; `cilium-dbg identity list` baseline.
- Run cilium preflight DaemonSet (image pre-pull + CNP validator) per upgrade guide.
- Confirm KubePrism healthy on all nodes (127.0.0.1:7445 LISTEN, KubePrismStatus).
- Confirm Flux Kustomization prune=false (it is) so a bad render can't delete CNI.
- Ensure scripts/cleanup-cilium-identities.sh is ready as a safety valve.
- Stage R1 values edit (deny serviceaccount label) in a branch, NOT applied yet.

STEPWISE (one minor at a time; each = helm/Flux chart bump + upgradeCompatibility):
1. 1.16.6 -> latest 1.16.x patch. Verify agents green, identity count flat.
2. -> latest 1.17.x (v1.17.18). Set upgradeCompatibility=1.16. Verify.
   Watch bpf-lb-proto-diff; smoke-test pihole LB + a ClusterIP.
3. Land R1 values edit (deny serviceaccount) + re-verify SPIRE volumes[3] index.
   -> 1.18.12. Set upgradeCompatibility=1.17. Verify enable-l2-neigh-discovery
   stays true; arping pihole VIP; check identity count did NOT spike.
   Update Cilium metrics in baseline-alerts. Delete stale ExternalWorkloads CRD.
Because it's Flux-managed: bump chart version in helmrelease.yaml + set
upgradeCompatibility in values per step; DO NOT set --reuse-values (Flux uses
valuesFrom, fine). maxUnavailable=1 already limits agent-rotation blast.

POST-UPGRADE VERIFY (each step):
- All cilium + cilium-envoy + operator pods Ready; no restart storm.
- `cilium status --brief`; connectivity: pod->pod, pod->svc(ClusterIP),
  LAN->pihole VIP (ARP), DNS resolution through Talos hostDNS.
- CiliumIdentity count within ~2x baseline (abort/rollback if climbing).
- Hubble relay/ui up, flows visible; grpc mTLS (SPIRE mutual auth) still passing.
- SPIRE agent no CrashLoop (token TTL patch intact).

ROLLBACK:
- Cilium supports rollback only one minor at a time; keep upgradeCompatibility.
- Flux prune=false means reverting helmrelease.yaml chart version + re-reconcile
  restores prior minor without resource deletion. Rollback the SAME step you
  just took; never skip a minor on the way down either.
- If identity storm starts: run cleanup-cilium-identities.sh + revert R1 posture.

STOP LINE: Do NOT advance to 1.19.x until #46010 fix (1.19.5+) is validated on a
throwaway Talos node — 1.19.3/1.19.4 brick host networking on our exact profile.

title: Cilium pod-startup apiserver-ClusterIP EPERM race (KSM canary)
description:
At pod startup, pods connecting to apiserver ClusterIP 10.96.0.1:443 before Cilium programs their endpoint get EPERM 'operation not permitted' (datapath drop). KSM surfaced this (1198 restarts) because it has no client-creation retry; loosened its probes as mitigation (commit 54cc474). Deeper fix: investigate Cilium endpoint-programming latency / kube-proxy-replacement service-backend readiness on workers (esp talos06), consider adding monitoring/KSM to the wedge-buster backstop (infrastructure/base/kube-system/wedge-buster/). Affects any pod that talks to the apiserver early in startup.

=====================================================================
RESEARCH (2026-08-08)
=====================================================================
Deployed: Cilium **1.16.6** (infrastructure/base/cilium/helmrelease.yaml pins chart 1.16.6), kubeProxyReplacement=true, socket-LB default-on, bpf.masquerade=true, k8sServiceHost=localhost:7445 (KubePrism). Talos 1.13.x / K8s v1.34.

ROOT MECHANISM (confirmed upstream, not a guess):
- The EPERM comes from Cilium's **socket-LB cgroup connect4 hook REJECTING the connect() syscall when the service->backend lookup finds no backend** for the ClusterIP at that instant. It is NOT a policy drop at the veth. Upstream considered this errno a bug and changed it EPERM -> EHOSTUNREACH in PR cilium/cilium#45185, shipped v1.19.4 / v1.20.0-pre.2 — precisely because apps treat EPERM as fatal (as KSM does). https://github.com/cilium/cilium/releases/tag/v1.19.4
- Windows where the LB-map entry for 10.96.0.1 is empty: sock-LB cgroup program re-attach + service resync during cilium-agent restart (matches "worsens during agent restarts"); single control-plane = exactly 1 backend, so any apiserver endpoint flap empties the service.
- Secondary contributor: new endpoints carry **reserved:init identity** until identity/labels resolve; if any policy selects the namespace, traffic is dropped until first regeneration completes. https://docs.cilium.io/en/stable/security/policy/lifecycle/ — identity/CEP churn (our TALOS-yyt bloat history) stretches this window. Related upstream: empty-policy-map-after-regeneration-retry race https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/38998 ; agent<->apiserver restart cascade https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/34653

RANKED REMEDIATIONS (impact x safety, single-CP Talos+KPR homelab):
1. **[LOW RISK — do first] Workload-side wait/retry for early-API pods** (KSM + anything hitting apiserver at t=0):
   - initContainer gate: `until wget -q --spider --no-check-certificate https://10.96.0.1:443/healthz; do sleep 1; done` (EPERM fails instantly, so the loop is cheap) — converts crashloop into a clean wait.
   - startupProbe with generous failureThreshold (partially done for KSM in 54cc474).
   - Add monitoring/KSM to wedge-buster backstop (original ticket idea) as belt-and-braces.
   - KSM upstream has a history of hard-fail-no-retry on client creation: https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-state-metrics/issues/542 , https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-state-metrics/issues/683
2. **[MEDIUM RISK — needed anyway] Upgrade Cilium 1.16.6 -> latest 1.18.x patch.** 1.16 is EOL and NOT in the K8s v1.34 compatibility matrix (1.34 pairs with 1.18.x+): https://docs.cilium.io/en/stable/network/kubernetes/compatibility/ . 1.17/1.18 carry KPR + endpoint-restore + service-sync fixes that narrow the race. **AVOID 1.19.3/1.19.4 on Talos for now**: confirmed regression — KPR kills Talos host networking during endpoint/veth/BPF init on Talos 1.13.2 (1.18.9 confirmed working there): https://github.com/cilium/cilium/issues/46010 . Note the errno fix (#45185, EPERM->EHOSTUNREACH) only lands in 1.19.4+, so on 1.18.x apps still see EPERM — item 1 stays necessary regardless.
3. **[LOW-MED RISK toggle] Enable CiliumEndpointSlice** (`ciliumEndpointSlice.enabled: true`) to cut CEP/identity apiserver churn that lengthens endpoint programming during agent restarts — directly relevant given the identity-bloat history. Roll during a quiet window (operator + agents restart).
4. **[KEEP AS-IS] `k8sServiceHost: localhost` / `k8sServicePort: 7445` (KubePrism)** is already the correct Talos pattern and breaks the cilium#41108 agent-bootstrap chicken-and-egg — but it protects the AGENT only, not workload pods (pods still resolve KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST to the ClusterIP through sock-LB). Talos guidance: https://docs.siderolabs.com/kubernetes-guides/cni/deploying-cilium
5. **[LOW RISK, conditional] Allow the `init` entity in any CiliumNetworkPolicy-covered namespaces** so pre-identity endpoints aren't policy-dropped during the reserved:init window: https://docs.cilium.io/en/stable/security/policy/lifecycle/
6. **[INVESTIGATED — NO-OPs for this bug, don't spend time]:** `cni.exclusive` (only controls wiping other CNI confs; CNI ADD already blocks sandbox creation until endpoint create — the residual window is identity + LB-map programming, which happens after ADD returns); `endpoint-gc-interval` (CEP garbage collection, not programming latency); `bpf.hostLegacyRouting` / `enableEndpointRoutes` (routing-path choice, unrelated to sock-LB reject); `socketLB.hostNamespaceOnly` (would swap fast EPERM for per-packet drops/timeouts — strictly worse); `enable-k8s-terminating-endpoint` (default true since 1.11, already active).
7. **[OBSERVABILITY] Alert on the signal, not the symptom:** Hubble drop metrics are already enabled — add PromQL alerts on `cilium_drop_count_total` (reason=Service/no-backend class) and on KSM container restart rate, so the next widening of this window pages before a 1198-restart pileup.

title: vpn-rotator: no floor on server exclusion — one bad run wedges the whole rotation fleet
description: When every ProtonVPN server lands in the failed_servers cooldown list (1h FAILED_SERVER_COOLDOWN), the rotator has zero candidates and every scheduled Job fails BackoffLimitExceeded until the cooldown expires ~1h later. Observed 2026-08-06: all 4 servers (nl/de/be/in) marked failed 22:08-22:10 (cascade from the empty-publicip validation bug + a DR-test canary transiently holding se-in-1/se-be-1), then jobs failed every 35min for >1h. A single bad run / transient / test should NOT be able to wedge the whole fleet. Fixes to consider: keep a floor (when all are cooled down, pick the least-recently-failed instead of erroring), don't count validation-only failures toward the hard cooldown, shorten cooldown, or add jitter/backoff caps. Depends on the validation fix (the root trigger). Evidence: rotation-state.json failed_servers all 4; rotator logs 'No healthy servers available! All 4 servers failed recently.'

title: SPIKE: pre-warmed VPN egress-gateway pool + route/proxy flip (zero-downtime rotation)
description: Alternative to control-API reconnect rotation (which briefly flaps the tunnel): run N always-on gluetun egress GATEWAY pods, one per ProtonVPN route/country (pre-warmed), each behind a stable Service, and rotate by FLIPPING which gateway a consumer routes through (instant, no tunnel setup). Two variants: (a) proxy-pointer flip (change HTTP/SOCKS proxy URL/Service selector — simple, app must honor proxy) vs (b) L3 default-route swap in the app netns (any app, needs policy routing / NET_ADMIN / routing sidecar). Constraints to evaluate: ProtonVPN concurrent-connection limit (=# distinct keys, currently 4: nl/de/be/in); kill-switch/leak — app pod has no VPN firewall so egress must be NetworkPolicy-locked to only the gateways or it can leak on gateway loss; long-lived connections still reset on flip (exit IP changes). Compare vs current per-pod sidecar. Prior art: CNI/cilium-layer routing was tried and abandoned (finicky) — sidecar/gateway is the blessed path.

title: Pi-hole DNS split: ~20% of queries served by ft6np (talos03), not just the mainline (talos06)
description:
The new 'DNS Served per Instance' panel revealed that TWO Pi-hole instances serve DNS concurrently, not single-active: fqzgm@talos06 ~1 q/s (mean 0.99) AND ft6np@talos03 ~0.2 q/s (mean 0.205, ~17-20% of traffic) all day. Others negligible.

ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis): the shared VIP 192.168.1.240 (LB-IPAM sharing-key 'pihole') has its two Cilium L2 announcement leases on DIFFERENT nodes — cilium-l2announce-pihole-pihole-dns=talos06, cilium-l2announce-pihole-pihole-web=talos03. So .240 is ARP-announced by both nodes; LAN clients resolve .240 to whichever node's MAC they cached, splitting DNS between talos06 (fqzgm) and talos03 (ft6np).

IMPACT: functionally OK (both instances have identical config/blocklists), but it's not the intended single-active + clean failover; per-client stats are split across two FTL DBs, and it complicates the 'active instance' mental model.

FIX DIRECTIONS: get both pihole-dns + pihole-web L2 announcements onto the SAME node (investigate Cilium L2 behavior with shared IPs across 2 services / sharing-key), or announce the shared VIP from a single L2 lease. Verify with the new dashboard panel (want ONE green line, others flat).
notes: Fix A applied 2026-08-06 (commit 478a22c): pihole-web -> ClusterIP. Verified: .240 now has a SINGLE l2announce lease (pihole-dns@talos06); web lease gone; DNS resolves via .240; web UI still served via Traefik. DNS split root cause removed. Watch the 'DNS Served per Instance' panel — ft6np should decay to ~0 as client ARP caches expire (few min). Close once the graph shows single-active.

title: vpn-rotator CronJob wedge: apk add hang, no activeDeadlineSeconds
description: Job vpn-rotator-29665655 has been running 54 days at 0/1 with pod pid1 stuck on 'apk add python3' (Alpine repo unreachable during that specific run). concurrencyPolicy: Forbid blocks every subsequent /35min schedule fire; kube-controller-manager fires TooManyMissedTimes warning each schedule window. Add activeDeadlineSeconds so future wedges self-heal; kill the current stuck job to unblock.
close_reason: Root cause: dtzar/helm-kubectl:latest ships without python and the CronJob installed it via 'apk add python3' at every run. A single failed apk fetch on 2026-05-28 wedged the job forever (pid1 sh sleeping on apk, concurrencyPolicy: Forbid blocked all subsequent /35min windows for 54d). Fix: (1) swap image to alpine/k8s:1.34.9 which pre-bakes python3 + kubectl + helm (matches cluster k8s minor); rotate.py only uses stdlib so no pip needed. (2) activeDeadlineSeconds: 1500 on the job spec as belt-and-braces so any future hang self-heals in 25min. Verified end-to-end via 'kubectl create job --from=cronjob/vpn-rotator …' — new job pulled the image, python3 launched immediately, rotate.py entered its normal jitter phase and started emitting JSON logs. Followup nice-to-have (not filed): rotate.py uses deprecated datetime.utcnow().

title: Investigate ongoing CiliumIdentity churn despite label filter (31 stale per 2h)
description:
## Why this issue exists

Per the 2026-05-30 pod-cleanup run, we're STILL accruing ~31 stale CiliumIdentities every 2 hours despite the TALOS-yyt label filter excluding the known high-churn label keys (controller-uid, pod-template-hash, batch.kubernetes.io/*, job-name, dagster/*, helm.sh/*, velero.io/*).

```
[INFO] CiliumIdentities: total=183 used=152 stale=31
[INFO] CiliumIdentities deleted: 31
Cilium identity status: WARNING (cleanup occurred — check label filter)
```

31 stale per 2h = ~370/day = ~2,600/week. Without the safety-net cron, we'd be back to meltdown territory in 2-3 weeks. The safety net is working but it's a symptom-cleanup, not a root-cause fix.

## Questions to answer

1. **Which labels are still creating identity churn?** Per-namespace breakdown:
   ```bash
   # Audit which label keys the *current* stale identities have
   kubectl get ciliumidentities -o json | \
     jq -r '.items[] | [.metadata.name, (.metadata.labels|to_entries|map(.key)|join(","))] | @tsv' \
     | head -50
   ```

2. **Is this driven by ephemeral Jobs/CronJobs?** Count of high-churn workloads:
   - Velero kopia-maintain jobs (5 backup namespaces × 3/day = 15/day)
   - Authentik postgres backup
   - Dagster step runs (catalyst-data namespace)
   - Pod-cleanup itself (every 2h)
   - kube-state-metrics scrape pods
   - Anything in `scratch/`

3. **Is our solution a correct bypass or are we doing something wrong?**
   Three possible paths forward:
   a. **Extend the denylist** with the actually-observed-churning label keys. Tactical but never-ending whack-a-mole.
   b. **Switch to a strict allowlist** in cilium-config (`labels: "^k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace$ ^k8s:app$ ..."`). Cleaner, but risks under-filtering legitimate identity dimensions.
   c. **Fix the upstream workloads** — Jobs/CronJobs SHOULD have stable identity-relevant labels. If a workload pattern is generating unique labels per-instance (random suffixes, timestamps), that's a workload bug.

4. **Are there workloads using non-deterministic labels for fields that should be stable?** Common offenders:
   - Manifests that template `metadata.labels.run-id: "{{ uuid }}"` or similar
   - Helm charts that include `.Release.Revision` in non-managed labels
   - Operators that synthesize labels from per-instance state (e.g., `dagster/run-id` which we already excluded)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Audit current stale identity composition (which labels are driving churn)
- [ ] Document top 3 sources of ongoing churn
- [ ] Decide on path: extend denylist, switch to allowlist, or fix workloads
- [ ] If allowlist: validate that no NetworkPolicies depend on labels we'd drop
- [ ] Measure post-fix: stale identities per 2h cron should drop to <5
- [ ] Update TALOS-yyt memory with findings

## Why this matters

The safety-net cron + alerts already prevent meltdowns. This is a "do it right" follow-up: understand what's actually happening so we're not relying on cleanup forever, and so a new noisy workload doesn't blindside us.

## Defer until

Cluster has been stable for 24h with the safety-net catching everything. Then investigate at leisure.
notes:
## Investigation findings (2026-05-30, sub-agent audit)

**Verdict: denylist is working correctly. The 31 stale/2h is NOT pollution — it's normal pod-restart churn.**

### Key findings

1. **All remaining labels on live identities are stable** — namespace, serviceaccount, cluster, app.kubernetes.io/*, kubevirt.io, etc. No high-churn labels are slipping through the filter.

2. **No workloads with bad label patterns found**. Unlike pre-fix Dagster (`run-id: <uuid>`), all current workloads use stable identity-relevant labels. Jobs correctly use `batch.kubernetes.io/job-name` (filtered), Velero uses `velero.io/repo-name` (filtered). No `run-id`/`instance-id`/`pod-hash-suffix` chaos.

3. **77 new identities in 24h, of which Mimir/monitoring drives 51% (44)**. With 14 live Mimir pods, that's ~1.7 new identities per pod per day = each pod restarted ~1.7x daily. This is just rolling updates from Flux HelmRelease + occasional OOM/eviction churn.

4. **The "31 stale per 2h" cron finding is misleading**: it counts identities that are momentarily orphaned during pod rollovers. Cilium's operator GC (15min) catches most of them; our 2h cron sweeps the remainder. That's not pollution accumulating — it's GC working as designed with a small lag.

### Action items (none urgent)

- [ ] **Quick win**: investigate why Mimir pods restart ~1.7x/day. Check OOM/eviction logs, consider raising memory limits or relaxing liveness probes.
- [ ] **Tweak alert semantics**: the safety-net cron's WARNING status will fire on every run because of this normal churn. Either lower the alert threshold or change the metric semantics so "WARNING" means "more stale than expected" (e.g., >50) not "any stale found".

### Re-classification

Not actually a problem — identity churn is at healthy baseline. Keep this issue OPEN as a tracking placeholder for the alert-semantics tweak in TALOS-cq7. Re-prioritize if churn climbs back above ~500/day.

title: capture-meltdown-evidence.sh: `timeout` not available on macOS — script silently fails
description:
## Why

Run during the 2026-05-29 3rd meltdown of the session. Script created `.output/incidents/20260529T181341Z/` with file stubs but all file contents are:

```
./scripts/capture-meltdown-evidence.sh: line 48: timeout: command not found
```

`timeout` is a GNU coreutils command, not present on macOS by default. The script was developed/tested on Linux and assumes coreutils.

## Fix

Replace the `run()` helper's `timeout 15 "$@"` with portable alternatives:

```sh
# Option A: detect and use gtimeout/timeout
if command -v gtimeout >/dev/null; then TIMEOUT_CMD=gtimeout
elif command -v timeout >/dev/null; then TIMEOUT_CMD=timeout
else TIMEOUT_CMD=""
fi
run() {
  local label=$1; shift
  local out=$1; shift
  echo "  - ${label}"
  if [ -n "$TIMEOUT_CMD" ]; then
    "$TIMEOUT_CMD" 15 "$@" > "${out}" 2>&1 || echo "  ⚠️  ${label} failed" >&2
  else
    "$@" > "${out}" 2>&1 || echo "  ⚠️  ${label} failed" >&2
  fi
}
```

Or `perl -e 'alarm shift @ARGV; exec @ARGV' 15 "$@"` (perl is everywhere).

## File

`scripts/capture-meltdown-evidence.sh` line 48 (the `run()` helper)

## Acceptance

- Script works on both macOS (default install) and Linux
- Verified by running on a healthy cluster from a macOS dev machine
- Files in output dir contain actual command output, not "command not found"
acceptance_criteria:
- Script tested on macOS, produces non-empty output files
- timeout/gtimeout detection works
- Falls back gracefully if neither is available

title: Investigate persistent Cilium agent failure on talos02-gpu (332 restarts in 38h post-kick)
description:
## Why

On 2026-05-29 cluster status check, `cilium-z9lzc` on `talos02-gpu` is in CrashLoopBackOff with **332 restarts in 38h** — it has been failing since we kicked it during the 2026-05-27 recovery. This is independent of the talos00 control-plane meltdowns; it's a sticky talos02-gpu specific issue.

Consequence: every pod on talos02-gpu can't reach in-cluster service IPs (10.96.0.1, etc.). cnpg has been crashlooping there for 7+ days (3135 restarts). The webhook live-patch (TALOS-ig6) hides this from the cluster but cnpg itself stays broken.

## What's special about talos02-gpu

- GPU node (Intel Arc, used for transcoding)
- Has intel-device-plugins running
- Likely runs Tdarr/Plex transcode workloads
- May have higher pod density / different driver kernel modules

## Diagnostics to capture (use `scripts/capture-meltdown-evidence.sh talos02-gpu`)

- `talosctl --nodes 192.168.1.144 dmesg | grep -iE 'oom|hung|cilium|bpf|intel|i915'`
- `kubectl describe pod -n kube-system cilium-z9lzc | tail -30` (startup probe failure reason)
- `kubectl logs -n kube-system cilium-z9lzc --previous | tail -100`
- Memory pressure: `talosctl read /proc/meminfo /proc/loadavg`
- Are there orphan BPF programs? `kubectl exec ... -- bpftool prog show | head`

## Likely fixes (try in order)

1. Reboot talos02-gpu (`talosctl reboot --nodes 192.168.1.144 --mode=force`). Clears BPF state.
2. If recurs after reboot: bump cilium memory limit per-node OR move GPU-heavy workloads off until investigated
3. Long-term: a different startup-probe configuration or node-specific cilium tuning

## Acceptance

- cilium-z9lzc transitions to 1/1 Running and stays for ≥1h
- cnpg on talos02-gpu recovers
- Root cause documented (was it BPF orphans, memory pressure, GPU driver interaction, ...?)
acceptance_criteria:
- Cilium agent on talos02-gpu stable ≥1h after fix
- cnpg pod (or whatever else is stuck there) recovers
- Root cause documented

title: Post-mortem doc: 2026-05-29 cluster meltdowns + cognitive council root cause
description:
## Why

The 2026-05-29 meltdown happened <24h after a different meltdown on 2026-05-27, and ~8 days after the original 2026-05-21 incident. Same symptom, same recovery. Cognitive council (4 expert subagents) tore apart the analysis and identified actual root causes vs. symptom treatment.

Document is essential to:
- Stop the on-call (me) from re-treating symptoms in the next incident
- Hand off to future contributors / sessions
- Prove whether/when each mitigation actually worked

## Document to create

`docs/06-troubleshooting/2026-05-29-network-meltdown.md` (mirroring the 2026-05-21 template).

### Required sections

1. **TL;DR** — what broke, when, how recovered
2. **Timeline** (UTC):
   - 2026-05-29 ~16:30 UTC: cluster API unreachable (`192.168.1.54:6443` timeout)
   - 16:50: identified cilium-eats-itself cascade, force-rebooted talos00
   - 17:00: cluster recovered, 3 broken operators recovered
   - 17:10 onwards: filed cognitive council, identified architectural root cause
3. **What the 4 council members found** (one paragraph each)
4. **Actual root cause** — single CP + workloads + kubeProxyReplacement is structurally fragile; recurring fsync from hourly etcd snapshot likely trigger; broken webhook configs amplify cascade
5. **What we did** — list every change with link to commit + beads issue
6. **What we explicitly did NOT do** — KubePrism switch (deferred to TALOS-kp-debug); kube-proxy hybrid (user vetoed); SPIRE disable (user vetoed)

title: Dual GitOps demarcation tuning — reduce ArgoCD watch overhead
description:
## Why

Per 2026-05-29 cognitive council: running BOTH Flux and ArgoCD on a single-CP cluster doubles list/watch traffic against the single apiserver. The architect specifically called this out as a "100% accelerant" of meltdowns (low probability as trigger, high impact when one happens).

User explicitly wants to KEEP dual GitOps because of clean separation:
- **Flux** → infrastructure (CNI, ingress, storage, observability, operators, secrets, DBs)
- **ArgoCD** → applications (arr stack, plex, catalyst-ui, dagster, MeTube, etc.)

That separation is healthy. The accelerant is reducible by tuning.

## Tuning levers

1. **ArgoCD `application.resourceTrackingMethod=annotation`** (instead of default `label`)
   - Each label-write triggers an etcd put; annotations are less hot
2. **ArgoCD `controller.resourceExclusions`** — exclude all the resource kinds Flux owns from ArgoCD's watch set
   - At minimum: `HelmRelease`, `Kustomization`, `GitRepository`, `OCIRepository`, `Bucket`, `Alert`, `Provider`, `Receiver`, `ImagePolicy`, `ImageRepository`, `ImageUpdateAutomation`
3. **ArgoCD `controller.repo.parallelism` / `application.controller.processors.operation` / `processors.status`**: tune down for homelab scale
4. **Flux already throttled**: `--concurrent=2 --kube-api-qps=20 --kube-api-burst=40` (commit a29010d). Confirm still appropriate.
5. **ArgoCD `application.sync.timeout`** — make it longer (less retry pressure)

## Demarcation audit

Walk the repo:
- `applications/` (Flux)? Should be empty or ArgoCD-pointed
- `infrastructure/base/argocd/applications/` — anything pointing at non-app stuff (eg infra) should move to Flux
- Decide what 'platform' edge cases live where (e.g. cert-manager — Flux; argocd itself — Flux; observability — Flux; arr — ArgoCD; plex — ArgoCD)

## Acceptance

- ArgoCD `resourceTrackingMethod: annotation` set
- ArgoCD `resourceExclusions` excludes all Flux CRDs
- Demarcation documented in `docs/02-architecture/dual-gitops.md`
- Apiserver watch metric (`apiserver_longrunning_gauge`) reduced after change (measure before/after)
acceptance_criteria:
- ArgoCD tuned per above
- Demarcation doc updated
- Before/after metric on apiserver watch count shows reduction

title: Debug why KubePrism (port 7445) is not actually listening despite enabled in machineconfig
description:
## Why

On 2026-05-29 we tried to switch Cilium's `k8sServiceHost` from the single-CP IP (192.168.1.54) to `localhost:7445` (Talos KubePrism) to decouple Cilium from a single point of failure. The change was reverted because verification showed:

```
talosctl --nodes <each-of-5-nodes> read /proc/net/tcp   # empty rows for port 7445
talosctl --nodes <each-of-5-nodes> read /proc/net/tcp6  # empty rows for port 7445
```

Nothing is actually listening on TCP/7445 on any of the 5 nodes (talos00/01/02-gpu/03/06).

**BUT** machineconfig says:
```yaml
kubePrism:
  enabled: true
  port: 7445
```
on all 5 nodes (verified via `talosctl get machineconfigs -o yaml`).

Known upstream issue: [siderolabs/talos#9132](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/issues/9132) — "Cilium install instructions incorrectly assume operational kubeprism" — describes exactly this: KubePrism configured but not listening, Cilium agents crashloop when pointed at it.

## What to investigate

1. Is the KubePrism listener bound to a specific interface (not 0.0.0.0/`::`)?
   - `talosctl --nodes <ip> read /proc/net/tcp` and `tcp6` — look for ANY row with port `0x1D1D` (7445), check the address column
2. Is KubePrism's service crashed?
   - Talos doesn't expose KubePrism as a service via `talosctl service` — it's internal to apid
   - Check `talosctl --nodes <ip> logs apid` for KubePrism errors
   - `talosctl --nodes <ip> dmesg | grep -i kubeprism`
3. Did KubePrism fail to start because of dependency on `trustd` / `apid` cert chain?
   - Search results suggested: "apid needs trustd to get its certificate signed, but with certain configurations there is no Talos control plane so there is no trustd, causing KubePrism to never start"
4. Is there a network policy or eBPF program blocking 7445?
5. Is `cluster.controlPlane.localAPIServerPort` actually 7445? Could be different.

## Fix paths (try in order)

1. `talosctl --nodes <ip> service apid restart` (cheap to try)
2. Re-apply machineconfig (`talosctl apply-config`) — sometimes forces re-init
3. Open issue upstream with our reproduction
4. Worst case: enable `cluster.allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes: true` + `proxy: { disabled: true }` and configure Cilium to point at the Talos VIP if we add one

## Acceptance

- KubePrism actually listens on 7445 on all 5 nodes (verifiable via `/proc/net/tcp` or curl from a host-net pod)
- Cilium safely switched to `k8sServiceHost: localhost`, `k8sServicePort: 7445` (canary on 1 worker first)
- All Cilium agents come up ready
- Document the fix in the post-mortem
acceptance_criteria:
- KubePrism listens on 7445 on every node (verified live)
- Cilium successfully switched to localhost:7445 (canary first, then all)
- All Cilium agents ready
- Root cause documented in post-mortem
close_reason: Closed via update

title: Runbook: post network maintenance (router/switch reboot) cluster health checklist
description:
## Why

On 2026-05-27 the user restarted the router/switches earlier in the day. That brief network partition put cilium agents on talos02-gpu and talos03 into a death loop they couldn't recover from. The cluster then degraded silently for hours until plex broke.

If we'd known to check, a 30-second `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=cilium` immediately after the maintenance would have caught it.

## Document to add

`docs/05-runbooks/post-network-maintenance.md`:

```markdown
# Post Network Maintenance Checklist

After restarting the router, switches, or any networking gear that the cluster depends on, run these checks IMMEDIATELY. Brief network partitions are the #1 trigger for Cilium agent death spirals on Talos.

## Quick Check (60 seconds)

\`\`\`bash
# 1. All cilium agents healthy?
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=cilium -o wide
# Expect: all 1/1 Running, no CrashLoopBackOff, restart counts not climbing

# 2. All nodes Ready?
kubectl get nodes

# 3. Any admission webhooks broken?
scripts/safe-restart-cilium.sh --dry-run   # the pre-flight does exactly this check

# 4. Quick canary test
kubectl run net-check --rm -it --restart=Never --image=busybox -- nslookup kubernetes.default
\`\`\`

## If Cilium Agents Are CrashLoopBackOff

\`\`\`bash
# Step 1: kick the failing pod (control plane MUST be healthy for this to work)
kubectl delete pod -n kube-system <bad-cilium-pod>

# Step 2: wait 60s, recheck. If still failing, reboot the node:
talosctl --talosconfig configs/talosconfig --nodes <node-ip> reboot --mode=force --wait

# Step 3: if control plane is unreachable too, see:
#   docs/06-troubleshooting/2026-05-21-cilium-cascading-meltdown.md
#   docs/06-troubleshooting/2026-05-27-network-maintenance-cilium-meltdown.md (TODO file this incident)
\`\`\`

## Pre-Maintenance (optional but recommended)

If you know ahead of time you're rebooting network gear:
- `task k8s:dump-state` (snapshot current state for comparison)
- Note current cilium restart counts so you can spot increases post-maintenance
```

## Also file the new post-mortem doc

`docs/06-troubleshooting/2026-05-27-network-maintenance-cilium-meltdown.md` — same template as the 2026-05-21 doc, documenting:
- Trigger: router/switch reboot
- Cascade: cilium startup loop on talos02-gpu/talos03 → operators on those nodes lose apiserver → webhooks broken → cluster-wide admission stall → control plane eventually went dark
- Recovery: force-reboot talos00, kick stuck cilium pods, observe operators recover
- Why prior fix wasn't enough: bumped liveness but startup probe was the killer

## Acceptance

- New runbook in docs/05-runbooks/
- New post-mortem in docs/06-troubleshooting/
- Linked from QUICKSTART.md or top-level README under "When things break"
acceptance_criteria:
- post-network-maintenance.md runbook exists and is linked from QUICKSTART/top README
- 2026-05-27 post-mortem doc filed alongside the 2026-05-21 one

title: Bump Cilium startupProbe.failureThreshold (current loops kill agent before /healthz binds)
description:
## Why

The 2026-05-22 fix (commit a29010d) bumped Cilium's **liveness** probe failureThreshold from 10 → 30 (15min grace). That helps once an agent is *running*. But on 2026-05-27 we still saw two cilium pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff with **906 startup probe failures** each.

The startup probe is what gates "agent is ready to serve liveness checks." When the agent restarts after a network blip, the startup probe runs **before** the agent's `/healthz` endpoint is bound. If the startup probe fails too many times, kubelet kills the pod → backs off → tries again → fails again → infinite loop. The agent never gets a chance to fully initialize.

Sample from `kubectl describe pod cilium-m8v8k`:
```
Warning  Unhealthy  19h (x906 over 5d12h)  kubelet  spec.containers{cilium-agent}: Startup probe failed: Get "http://127.0.0.1:9879/healthz": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:9879: connect: connection refused
Warning  BackOff    19h (x500 over 5d12h)  kubelet  spec.containers{cilium-agent}: Back-off restarting failed container cilium-agent in pod cilium-m8v8k_kube-system
```

## Fix

In `configs/cilium-values.yaml`:

```yaml
startupProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: 9879
    scheme: HTTP
    httpHeaders:
      - name: brief
        value: "true"
  failureThreshold: 105   # current default is 105 (15.75 min @ 10s period)... actually verify current
  periodSeconds: 10
  successThreshold: 1
  timeoutSeconds: 5
```

But first **verify what the current live setting is**:
```
kubectl get ds -n kube-system cilium -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[?(@.name=="cilium-agent")].startupProbe}'
```

If it's already at the Cilium default of `failureThreshold: 105`, then the issue isn't probe tolerance — it's something else (e.g. apiserver unreachable from the pod). In that case, the fix is to make the agent more resilient to apiserver hiccups during init OR add a sidecar that delays the probe.

## Notes

- Don't blindly bump — verify root cause first. If apiserver was genuinely unreachable for 5 days, no probe tolerance bump will help.
- Related: cilium v1.16.6 is what we run. Check upgrade path to v1.16.x latest (NOT 1.18.8 — see cilium#45208 regression).

## Acceptance

- Current startup probe values documented
- If too aggressive, bumped with reasoning
- Synthetic test: simulate network partition (drop apiserver traffic for 90s), confirm cilium pod survives
acceptance_criteria:
- Current startup probe config documented
- Investigation determines whether probe tuning is the right fix or something else
- If a tuning change is made, recovery from a simulated 90s network partition verified

title: Route desec-ddns through ProtonVPN gluetun
description:
Currently desec-ddns publishes the home WAN IP (108.64.138.156) to kelsboi.dedyn.io. User wants the site to be seen as hosted through the VPN router for kelsboi.dedyn.io traffic.

## Approach options

### Option A: ProtonVPN port-forward (preferred)
- Add gluetun sidecar to desec-ddns pod (or move desec-ddns container into the existing vpn-gateway/gluetun pod as another sidecar)
- ddns-updater queries ipify.org through the tunnel → gets the ProtonVPN exit IP
- Publishes that IP to deSEC for kelsboi.dedyn.io
- ProtonVPN port-forwarding allocates a public port pointing back into gluetun
- Need to capture the rotating port via gluetun control API at http://localhost:8000/v1/openvpn/portforwarded
- Inbound flow: deSEC A record (VPN IP) → ProtonVPN port-forwarded port → gluetun → cluster

## Things to figure out
1. **Port forwarding rotation** — ProtonVPN rotates the forwarded port periodically. Need either:
   - A sidecar that reads gluetun's control API and re-publishes the port via SRV record (complex)
   - Or assume the same port + accept that connectivity is best-effort
2. **TLS / cert issuance** — Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 won't work over an arbitrary port. cert-manager already uses Cloudflare DNS-01 for the knowledgedump.space cert. Need to ensure kelsboi.dedyn.io certs use deSEC DNS-01 (deSEC supports it).
3. **Server selection** — only certain ProtonVPN servers (CH/IS/SE/RO) support port-forwarding
4. **Routing inbound traffic** — gluetun's iptables need to forward the inbound port to a Service IP within the cluster (Traefik's :443?)
5. **Testing** — verify with curl --resolve that the VPN IP path works

## Refs
- Existing gluetun setup: infrastructure/base/vpn-gateway/deployment.yaml (vpn-rotator)
- desec-ddns pod: external-dns/desec-ddns (deployed by talos-private/external-dns-desec/ddns.yaml)
- ProtonVPN port forwarding gluetun docs: https://github.com/qdm12/gluetun-wiki/blob/main/setup/providers/protonvpn.md

## Out of scope (not for this ticket)
- Cloudflare external-dns for knowledgedump.space (separate, already enabled this session)
- Migrating qbittorrent / arr-stack to use the same VPN routing path

Discovered: 2026-05-10

title: knowledge-graph-api crashes with empty Neo4j schema
description:
Pod catalyst-data/knowledge-graph-api in CrashLoopBackOff (127 restarts/10h). Logs show:

  [graphql-api] Connecting to Neo4j at bolt://neo4j.catalyst-data.svc.cluster.local:7687 ...
  [graphql-api] Neo4j connectivity OK.
  [graphql-api] Introspecting Neo4j schema ...
  [graphql-api] Introspection complete (39 chars of SDL).
  [graphql-api] Startup failed: Error: Type Query must define one or more fields.

Root cause: chicken-and-egg — the GraphQL API uses @neo4j/graphql introspection to auto-generate its schema from existing nodes/relationships. With an empty Neo4j (post UPS-2026-05-09 PV recovery), no schema is generated, Apollo Server refuses to start.

Fix options (all in external catalyst-data repo, github.com:TheBranchDriftCatalyst/catalyst-data):
1. Make the API tolerant of empty schemas (define a placeholder Type Query before introspection)
2. Pre-populate Neo4j with a minimal seed node so introspection produces a valid schema
3. Add an init container that runs a Cypher seed script before the API starts
