title: Restore synology-666 volume mounts for tdarr-server/worker
description:
When fixing arr-stack-private ArgoCD sync, tdarr-patches/kustomization.yaml was changed from resources: to patches: (UPS-2026-05-09 recovery). The strategic merge patches now silently drop because the target resources (tdarr-server Deployment, tdarr-worker DaemonSet) live in the public arr-stack repo, not this kustomization tree.

Result: synology-666 volumeMount/volume additions are NO LONGER reaching the cluster. Tdarr can no longer transcode private media on the synology /666 share.

Fix options:
1. Include the upstream arr-stack base as remote kustomize resource so patches have targets
2. Move synology-666 volume additions to the public arr-stack repo (cleaner — no cross-repo dependency)
3. Use ArgoCD spec.source.kustomize.patches field so ArgoCD applies the patches via SSA against in-cluster objects

Recommend option 2 (move to public repo) for simplicity.

Repo: github.com:TheBranchDriftCatalyst/private at tdarr-patches/
notes:
**VERIFIED 2026-05-22**: Public base path and container indexes corrected.

## Verified facts from public talos-homelab repo

- **Path**: `applications/tdarr/base/` (NOT `applications/arr-stack/base/tdarr/`)
- **Namespace**: `tdarr`
- **Server**: Deployment `tdarr-server`, containers[]:
  - `[0]` flow-importer (init-style, do NOT patch)
  - `[1]` **tdarr** ← patch volumeMounts here
- **Worker**: DaemonSet `tdarr-worker`, containers[]:
  - `[0]` **tdarr-node** ← patch volumeMounts here
- Existing volumes in both already include `synology-movies` + `synology-tv`,
  synology-666 will be a 3rd alongside them.

## Corrected kustomization for talos-private/tdarr-patches/

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: tdarr   # NOTE: not "media"

resources:
  # Pull public tdarr base. Pin to a specific commit for stability instead
  # of ?ref=main — upgrade deliberately when public base changes.
  - github.com/TheBranchDriftCatalyst/talos-homelab//applications/tdarr/base?ref=<commit-or-tag>
  # If synology-666 PVC isn't already present in cluster, define here:
  # - pvc-synology-666.yaml

patches:
  # tdarr-server (Deployment): add synology-666 mount to containers[1]=tdarr
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
      name: tdarr-server
    patch: |
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/containers/1/volumeMounts/-
        value:
          name: synology-666
          mountPath: /mnt/synology-666
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/volumes/-
        value:
          name: synology-666
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: synology-666

  # tdarr-worker (DaemonSet): add synology-666 mount to containers[0]=tdarr-node
  - target:
      kind: DaemonSet
      name: tdarr-worker
    patch: |
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/volumeMounts/-
        value:
          name: synology-666
          mountPath: /mnt/synology-666
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/volumes/-
        value:
          name: synology-666
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: synology-666
```

## Validate post-deploy

```bash
kubectl get deploy -n tdarr tdarr-server -o yaml | \
  yq '.spec.template.spec.containers[1].volumeMounts'
# Expect: config, server, logs, flows, synology-movies, synology-tv, synology-666

kubectl get ds -n tdarr tdarr-worker -o yaml | \
  yq '.spec.template.spec.containers[0].volumeMounts'
# Expect: node-info, transcode-cache, dri, synology-movies, synology-tv, synology-666

# Inside the pods, ls /mnt/synology-666 should show the share
kubectl exec -n tdarr deploy/tdarr-server -c tdarr -- ls /mnt/synology-666 | head -5
```

title: Migrate scratch-mongodb from NFS to local-path SC
description:
MongoDB's WiredTiger storage engine corrupts on NFS during unclean shutdowns (UPS-2026-05-09 incident).

Root cause:
- Single-replica StatefulSet means no peer to recover from — only option after corruption is full data wipe
- mongo on NFS is generally discouraged due to fsync/locking semantics issues
- Combined with NFS provisioner archiveOnDelete bug (separate ticket), recovery is painful

Recommendations (pick one):
A) Switch StatefulSet to local-path SC (simplest)
B) Add 2nd replica for HA so peer can resync after corruption
C) Both A and B for max safety

Tradeoff for option A:
- local-path means data lives on a single node
- Lose the node = lose the data
- But this IS the 'scratch' namespace, so acceptable

File location: applications/scratch/.../mongodb (find it via grep for the StatefulSet)

Discovered: 2026-05-09 (UPS recovery incident)

title: NFS provisioner archiveOnDelete=true not working — old data persists across PVC recreate
description:
HelmRelease at infrastructure/base/storage/nfs-provisioner/helmrelease.yaml sets archiveOnDelete: true, but during UPS-2026-05-09 recovery, deleting a PVC and recreating it left ALL old data in place.

Verified via direct NFS mount: 535MB of old data persisted after PVC delete/recreate.

Impact:
- This silently caused mongodb to repeatedly hit WT_PANIC on the corrupted data even after the PVC was 'wiped'
- Operators have a false sense that PVC deletion = data wipe

Workaround used during recovery:
- Manually wipe NFS subdirectory contents via debug pod with: find . -mindepth 1 -delete

Investigation needed:
1. Is archiveOnDelete actually wired up correctly in the helm chart?
2. Compare deployed helm chart values vs. what's in helmrelease.yaml
3. Consider switching to 'archive' strategy with cleanup CronJob instead
4. Document expected behavior so we don't get bit again

title: Velero PrometheusRule: alert on missing PodVolumeBackups in fs-backup runs
description:
Sister to TALOS-a8g's etcd-backup PrometheusRule. The 2026-05-09 audit revealed Velero ran 'successfully' but produced zero PodVolumeBackup CRs because pods were excluded. A success-by-itemcount alert would have missed this.

Add alerts:

title: Migrate Home Assistant recorder off NFS-backed SQLite
description:
Home Assistant's `/config` volume is NFS-backed (`fatboy-nfs-appdata`, PVC `homeassistant-config-nfs`). The SQLite recorder database (`home-assistant_v2.db`) on NFS causes:

1. **SIGBUS crashes**: `Fatal Python error: Bus error` during SQLAlchemy recorder commits — SQLite's mmap + NFS coherency is a known-bad combo
2. **Liveness probe kills**: NFS latency spikes stall the asyncio event loop → `GET /` probe times out → kubelet kills pod (exit 137)
3. **69 restarts** accumulated, most recent 2026-04-08

A probe relaxation was applied as a bandaid (`66be6c8` — loosened liveness from ~150s to ~600s kill window), but the fundamental issue remains: SQLite on NFS is unsafe.

Options (pick one):
A) **Migrate recorder to external DB**: Add `recorder.db_url: postgresql://...` to HA's `configuration.yaml`, pointing at a dedicated postgres instance (could reuse cloudnative-pg in the `databases` namespace). This is the HA-recommended approach for anything beyond a single SD card.
B) **Move /config to local-path PVC**: Preserves SQLite but puts it on local disk. Downside: node-pinned, need Velero backups for persistence across node failures.
C) **Hybrid**: local-path PVC for the SQLite DB file only (via a separate volume mount at `/config/.storage/`), keep the rest of /config on NFS for cross-node access.

Also noted:
- HA container has **no memory limit** (only request 512Mi, currently using ~450Mi). Consider adding `limits.memory: 2Gi` to prevent unbounded growth.
- HA logs to `/config/home-assistant.log` on disk, not stdout. Add `HASS_LOG_TO_STDOUT=1` for better k8s-native log access.

Deployment file: `applications/home-automation/base/homeassistant/deployment.yaml`
PVC file: `applications/home-automation/base/homeassistant/pvc.yaml`
close_reason: Deployed dedicated postgres:15-alpine in home-automation namespace (postgres.yaml). Configured HA recorder to use postgresql:// via configmap + init-container patch. Verified: 13 recorder tables created in postgres, HA serving web UI, 0 restarts. Tightened liveness probe timings now that SQLite-on-NFS root cause is eliminated. Old SQLite DB remains on NFS as backup. Commit 7f44c81.

title: Apply otel-operator leaderElection.enabled=false to stop restart flapping
description:
The `monitoring/opentelemetry-operator` manager container has accumulated 2070+ restarts because it exits on leader election lease loss (controller-runtime default behavior). Any brief API server network blip (~20s) causes the lease renewal to time out → exit code 1 → kubelet restart. ~34 flaps/day historically.

Root cause confirmed from previous-container logs showing:
```
failed to renew lease monitoring/9f7554c3.opentelemetry.io: timed out waiting for the condition
"problem running manager", "error": "leader election lost"
```

NOT OOM (exit code 1, not OOMKilled). Resources are chart defaults: requests 100m/64Mi, limits 100m/128Mi — adequate.

Since this is a single-replica deployment with no HA coordination needed, disabling leader election eliminates the failure path entirely.

Fix: edit `infrastructure/base/monitoring/v2-otel/operators/otel-operator/helmrelease.yaml`, add under `values`:
```yaml
manager:
  leaderElection:
    enabled: false
```

This will trigger a pod rollout. Apply during a quiet period since the pod is currently stable (last restart 2026-04-08). Upstream reference: open-telemetry/opentelemetry-operator#2460.

Current resources (chart defaults):
- manager: requests cpu=100m mem=64Mi, limits cpu=100m mem=128Mi
- kube-rbac-proxy: requests cpu=5m mem=64Mi, limits cpu=500m mem=128Mi
close_reason: Applied leaderElection.enabled=false in helmrelease.yaml. Pod rolled out with 0 restarts (5 transient restarts during rollout due to ServiceMonitor conflict, resolved by deleting stale ServiceMonitor). New pod running 2/2 on talos06.

title: Fix catalyst-data PVC accessModes mismatch blocking ArgoCD sync
description:
The `catalyst-data` ArgoCD application is stuck OutOfSync/Degraded because two PVCs cannot be patched to their desired access mode:

- `catalyst-data/metube-downloads`: live = `ReadOnlyMany`, git = `ReadWriteMany`
- `catalyst-data/tubesync-downloads`: same mismatch

PVC `spec.accessModes` is immutable after creation, so ArgoCD retries patches forever and logs:

    PersistentVolumeClaim "tubesync-downloads" is invalid: spec: Forbidden: spec is immutable after creation except resources.requests and volumeAttributesClassName for bound claims

The underlying PVs (`catalyst-data-metube-downloads`, `catalyst-data-tubesync-downloads`) are NFS-backed, already `ReadWriteMany`, and have `persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain`, so data is safe to preserve across a PVC delete+recreate.

Source of truth: `catalyst-data/k8s/storage/nfs-media-volumes.yaml` in the `catalyst-data` repo.

Discovered 2026-04-11 during cluster health pass — not blocking any currently-running workload (dagster media-ingest is using the existing ROX PVCs fine today), but keeps the argo app red and prevents further changes from syncing cleanly.
design:
Delete + recreate cycle, preserving data via Retain PVs:

1. Identify consumers:
   ```
   kubectl get pods -n catalyst-data -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.volumes[]?.persistentVolumeClaim.claimName | test("metube-downloads|tubesync-downloads")) | .metadata.name'
   ```
   Plus check k8sRunLauncher job template in `dagster-instance.yaml` for any job-level consumers.

2. Scale consuming deployments to 0 (at minimum `media-ingest`).

3. Delete both PVCs:
   ```
   kubectl delete pvc -n catalyst-data metube-downloads tubesync-downloads
   ```
   PVs will go to `Released`.

4. Clear claimRef so PVs return to `Available`:
   ```
   kubectl patch pv catalyst-data-metube-downloads --type=json -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/claimRef"}]'
   kubectl patch pv catalyst-data-tubesync-downloads --type=json -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/claimRef"}]'
   ```

5. Trigger ArgoCD sync — it will create new PVCs from git, which should bind to the existing PVs via `spec.volumeName`.

6. Verify `kubectl get pvc -n catalyst-data` shows RWX and Bound.

7. Scale consumers back up.

Alternative considered: manual `volumeName`-less PVCs that dynamic-provision fresh NFS volumes — rejected because it would orphan existing data on the NAS.
acceptance_criteria:
- `kubectl get application -n argocd catalyst-data` reports `Synced` and `Healthy`
- Both PVCs show `RWX` in `kubectl get pvc -n catalyst-data`
- `media-ingest` and any other consuming pods are Running
- No data loss on the NFS server (verify `/volume1/appdata/downloads/metube-downloads` and `tubesync-downloads` still contain pre-fix files)
close_reason: Fixed live: scaled down data-explorer + media-ingest, deleted both PVCs (metube-downloads, tubesync-downloads), cleared claimRef on the NFS-backed PVs so they went Available, triggered argocd hard refresh + sync, PVCs were recreated from git with ReadWriteMany and re-bound to the existing Retain PVs (no data loss), scaled consumers back up. catalyst-data argocd app is now Synced. Verified both PVCs show RWX and both pods are Running.

title: Back-propagate the reflector cross-ns secret pattern across the app

Replace ad-hoc duplication with reflector annotations (source secret: reflection-allowed/-namespaces + reflection-auto-enabled/-namespaces). Reduces drift + single source of truth. Enumerate candidates first, then convert incrementally.

title: Auto-link CNPG Postgres clusters into dbgate as predefined connections
description: dbgate supports predefined connections via env: CONNECTIONS=<ids> + CONNECTION_<id>_DRIVER/SERVER/PORT/USER/PASSWORD/LABEL. title: NFD master/worker high restart churn
description: node-feature-discovery-master ~772 restarts and each node-feature-discovery-worker ~1300 restarts over ~63d (~12-20/day). notes: ROOT CAUSE: NFD v0.17.4 treats transient kube-API VIP (10.96.0.1:443) loss as FATAL. NOT OOM (limits 4Gi master/512Mi worker; Last State=Error not OOMKilled), NOT probe-flapping (no probe-fail events). Worker exits 1 on 'no route to host' getting own pod for ownerReference. Master exits 2 via SIGSEGV nil-deref in leader-election shutdown path (NamespaceLister.stop) — and runs -enable-leader-election despite replicaCount=1 (pure downside). CHURN ALREADY STOPPED: all restart counts froze 2026-07-06 ~16:33 (one cluster-wide API/Cilium blip), clean 26d since; benign (labels persist). Fragility remains for next blip. FIX OPTIONS: A) bump chart 0.17.*->0.18.* (addresses both, confidence med on worker path); B) Flux postRenderer stripping -enable-leader-election from single-replica master (deterministic master fix, worker still restarts benignly on 0.17.x). Do NOT raise mem/loosen probes.
close_reason: Fixed via chart bump 0.17.x->0.18.3. Root cause: NFD v0.17.4 fatal-on-transient-API-loss (worker exit1; master SIGSEGV in leader-election shutdown). Churn was already dormant (froze 26d ago after one Jul-6 blip). Verified: all 6 NFD pods rolled to v0.18.3, 0 restarts, HelmRelease Ready, NodeFeatureRule + gpu/gpu-arc labels survived, tdarr workers healthy.

title: Talos nodeLabels not reconciling on worker nodes
description: machine.nodeLabels in Talos worker configs (node.kubernetes.io/workload-type, topology.kubernetes.io/zone, node-role.kubernetes.io/worker) never appear on the K8s Node objects. Verified on talos06 + talos02-gpu: labels present in live machineconfig (talosctl get mc) but absent from 'kubectl get node'. node-role.kubernetes.io/* is expected (reserved prefix Talos drops), but the non-reserved ones should apply and don't. A custom homelab.dj/gpu-worker test label patched live also never appeared. Root-cause: Talos version (1.13.2) behavior, kubelet NodeRestriction, or a feature gate. Not urgent — no workload currently depends on Talos-set nodeLabels (tdarr migrated to NFD gpu-arc label in TALOS-ea6). Discovered during TALOS-ea6.
notes: ROOT CAUSE: Talos k8s.NodeApplyController submits ALL machine.nodeLabels as ONE atomic Node update using the node's kubelet identity (system:node:<name>). kube-apiserver NodeRestriction (confirmed enabled) rejects the WHOLE update because it contains node-role.kubernetes.io/* labels (worker, gpu-worker) which a node may never self-assign. Atomic = the permitted labels (node.kubernetes.io/workload-type, topology.kubernetes.io/zone, *-model) are collateral damage and never persist either. Proof: machined logs show 'NodeApplyController failed: nodes talosNN is forbidden: is not allowed to modify labels: node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu-worker, node-role.kubernetes.io/worker' retrying ~60s. gpu-model on talos06 is an orphan manual kubectl label, not proof Talos works (siblings absent). FIX: remove node-role.kubernetes.io/{worker,gpu-worker} from machine.nodeLabels on ALL workers (talosctl patch mc, NO reboot); permitted labels land next reconcile. Do NOT re-add role labels to config (use kubectl one-shot or Talos CCM if ROLES column wanted). Reboot does NOT help. Adjacent: taint regression siderolabs/talos#13443 on v1.13.3.
close_reason: Fixed. Root cause: atomic NodeApply rejected wholesale by NodeRestriction because machine.nodeLabels contained node-role.kubernetes.io/{worker,gpu-worker}, poisoning all permitted labels. Stripped node-role labels from live machineconfigs on talos01/02-gpu/03/06 via talosctl patch mc (no reboot). Verified: NodeApplyController errors stopped, and workload-type/zone/*-model labels now land on all 4 workers for the first time. Synced gitignored local config files. Role labels intentionally NOT re-added (would re-poison); use kubectl/Talos CCM out-of-band if ROLES column wanted.

title: etcd-backup CronJob: prune command broken (awk missing in minio/mc image, 312 snapshots accumulated)
description:
## Why

Discovered during the 2026-05-29 manual snapshot trigger test. The `upload` container of `etcd-backup` runs `mc` (minio/mc image) for S3 upload + retention pruning, but the prune step uses `awk` which isn't in the minio/mc image:

```
[*] Pruning to last 168...
/bin/sh: line 18: awk: command not found
[*] Done. Total snapshots: 312
```

Retention is `RETENTION_COUNT: "168"` (1 week at hourly) but we have **312 snapshots** in S3. This isn't causing cluster impact (S3 is fine), but it IS quietly violating the retention policy.

## Fix options

1. Replace awk with mc's own listing/sort + jq/grep tail:
   ```sh
   mc ls --json "${S3_DIR}" | jq -r '.key' | sort | head -n "${to_delete}"
   ```
   (jq is also not in minio/mc... so really only `sort | head` portable tools)

2. Add a tiny image with both tools (busybox-multi-arch + mc)

3. Use `mc ilm` (information lifecycle management) on the bucket to auto-prune by age — proper S3-native retention. Much cleaner.

**Recommended: option 3** (mc ilm).

## File

`infrastructure/base/backup/etcd-backup.yaml` lines ~119-130

## Acceptance

- Prune works (either via fixed script or mc ilm)
- Backup count stays at or below RETENTION_COUNT
- Verify by checking S3 backup count over 7 days
acceptance_criteria:
- Snapshot count stays ≤ RETENTION_COUNT after fix
- No prune errors in next 7 runs of the CronJob

title: Re-enable Cilium ClusterMesh when federation peer cluster goes live
description:
## Why

`configs/cilium-values.yaml` line ~234 has `clustermesh.apiserver.replicas: 0` as of 2026-05-29. We scaled it down because:
- It was running 3 containers (etcd + apiserver + kvstoremesh) pinned to the control-plane via `requiredDuringScheduling` nodeAffinity
- `enable-external-workloads=false` — no peer cluster registered yet
- Its embedded etcd was contributing to control-plane load and likely a meltdown trigger
- The whole 4-day-meltdown cycle was partly attributable to this overload

## What to do when bringing federation live

1. Confirm the AWS lighthouse peer cluster is actually ready (certs valid, NodePort 32379 reachable from peer side via Nebula IP `10.100.2.1`)
2. **Before scaling back to 1**: re-evaluate the nodeAffinity pin to control-plane.
   - Original justification: NodePort 32379 needs to be at Nebula IP `10.100.0.1` (only on talos00)
   - After **TALOS-ha-cp** lands and all 3 CPs have Nebula, this pin can be removed (clustermesh-apiserver can run on any CP, NodePort still routes correctly)
   - Until then, keep the pin but acknowledge the load it adds
3. Scale to 1: `clustermesh.apiserver.replicas: 1`
4. Render manifests, helm apply (Cilium is not in GitOps — see TALOS-cilium-gitops)
5. Verify cross-cluster pod-to-pod connectivity works
6. Update ADR / docs

## Acceptance

- Federation peer cluster verified ready
- clustermesh-apiserver scaled back to 1 in `configs/cilium-values.yaml`
- Cross-cluster connectivity verified
- Monitoring includes ClusterMesh API health alert
acceptance_criteria:
- Federation peer (aws-lighthouse) actually exists and TLS handshakes succeed
- clustermesh-apiserver: replicas=1 + cross-cluster pod ping works
- Decision made on nodeAffinity (keep / remove based on HA state)

title: Auto-heal stuck Cilium agents — START IN DRY-RUN (Discord notify only, no delete)
description:
## Why

Today's recovery was 80% "delete the cilium pod and let it restart" — once the control plane was healthy, the fresh cilium pods came up clean on the first try. This pattern is mechanical enough to automate.

## ⚠️ DEPLOYMENT STRATEGY: Dry-run first

**Phase 1 (initial deployment):** DRY-RUN MODE — observe-only.
- CronJob runs every 5 min
- Evaluates would-heal candidates (same logic as Phase 2)
- Posts to Discord: "🔍 [DRY-RUN] would have deleted pod `cilium-XXX` on `talos02-gpu` (CrashLoopBackOff 23m, restarts 47). All safety gates passed."
- Does NOT actually call `kubectl delete`
- Toggle via `DRY_RUN=true` env var on the CronJob (default: true)

**Phase 2 (after we trust the logic):** ACTIVE MODE — flip `DRY_RUN=false` after observing dry-run notifications for at least a week and confirming:
- No false positives (didn't propose deletes during a real meltdown)
- Detection threshold is right (not too eager, not too slow)
- Discord notifications are readable and actionable

## What it should do

A CronJob (every 5 min) that:
1. Checks all cilium-agent pods
2. If any pod has been in CrashLoopBackOff > 15 minutes AND its restart count is climbing AND **the control plane is reachable** (don't make a partition worse), it would `kubectl delete pod` (but in dry-run, just logs/notifies)
3. Always logs to Discord via the existing notification system:
   - Dry-run: "🔍 [DRY-RUN] Would heal `cilium-XXX` on `nodeY` (CrashLoopBackOff Zm, NN restarts). Safety gates: ✓ CP reachable, ✓ Only 1 pod unhealthy, ✓ Not recently healed."
   - Active mode (later): "🔧 Auto-healed `cilium-XXX` on `nodeY` (was in CrashLoopBackOff for Zm)"
   - Always: "🚫 Skipped heal of `cilium-XXX` because <safety gate that failed>"

## Safety gates (CRITICAL — these MUST work correctly in dry-run before activating)

- Skip if `kubectl get --raw /readyz` doesn't return 200
- Skip if any apiserver static pod has a recent (<5m) restart
- Skip if MORE than 1 cilium pod is unhealthy (smells like network meltdown — needs human)
- Max 1 deletion per cron run
- Rate-limit: don't delete the same pod twice within 30 min (in dry-run: don't re-notify about the same pod within 30 min)

## Files

`infrastructure/base/monitoring/cilium-self-heal/cronjob.yaml` (new dir)
- ConfigMap with the shell script (or small Go binary baked into image)
- ServiceAccount + RBAC: get/list pods in kube-system, delete pods in kube-system, get /readyz
- CronJob with env vars: `DRY_RUN=true`, `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_SECRET=discord-webhook`, thresholds

## Acceptance

- Phase 1: CronJob deployed in dry-run, posts to Discord on its first eligible evaluation
- Safety gates verified by simulating apiserver unreachable → CronJob skips and notifies "🚫 Skipped — CP unreachable"
- Dry-run notifications run for ≥1 week with no false positives before flipping DRY_RUN to false
- Phase 2 toggle is a 1-line env var change (no logic change)
- Documentation explains how to toggle and how to permanently disable
acceptance_criteria:
- Phase 1: CronJob deployed in DRY-RUN mode, posts to Discord on first eligible evaluation
- Phase 1: Safety gate test passes (simulate apiserver unreachable → CronJob skips & notifies)
- Phase 1: ≥1 week observation with no false positives before considering Phase 2
- Phase 2: 1-line env var toggle to activate, no code/logic change
- Documentation includes both toggle and permanent-disable instructions

title: Add non-root USER to tools/carrierarr/Dockerfile
description:
carrierarr's Dockerfile runs as root in the final image — no `USER` instruction in the runtime stage. Add a non-root user (uid 10001, no shell) and chown the /app directory accordingly.

Snippet to add before ENTRYPOINT:
```
RUN addgroup -g 10001 -S carrierarr && \
    adduser -u 10001 -S -G carrierarr carrierarr && \
    chown -R carrierarr:carrierarr /app
USER carrierarr
```

Verify the runtime deps (aws-cli, openssh-client) work as non-root — they should, but test before shipping. Drop CAP_NET_BIND if container is using port < 1024 (it's not — 8090 — so no concern).

Also consider for the same Dockerfile:
- Add BuildKit cache mount for `go mod download` (10x faster repeated builds)
- Audit .dockerignore in repo root

Discovered during TALOS-r5w (multi-stage-dockerfile skill smoke-test).
acceptance_criteria: Image rebuilds, container starts non-root (verify with `docker run --rm carrierarr id`), health check passes, no permission errors in logs.
